Verstappen finished in third, although he was suffering with engine-braking problems. Hamilton, too, made a late pass to claim fourth , with Lando Norris in fifth for McLarenThe race belonged to Antonelli, however. He did not put a foot wrong with a cool-headed display as he assuredly put one hand on the title. The Italianwent into the weekend insistinghe just wanted to have fun, to perform at his best and without letting the title play on his mind. He did so with no little success.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe pole lap had been brilliant, his first since Belgium in July, and in the race he demonstrated the same imperious form as when at his very best this season and which has brought him to within touching distance of his record-breaking achievement.Quick GuideHow the title races standShowDrivers' standings1Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes365pts2George Russell 🇬🇧Mercedes2423Lewis Hamilton 🇬🇧Ferrari2414Max Verstappen 🇳🇱Red Bull2365Charles Leclerc 🇲🇨Ferrari2336Lando Norris 🇬🇧McLaren2117Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren1448Isack Hadjar🇫🇷Red Bull1059Liam Lawson🇳🇿Racing Bulls7710Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine4211Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls3812Franco Colapinto🇦🇷Alpine2713Oliver Bearman 🇬🇧Haas2314Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi1315Gabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷Audi1016Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas717Fernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston Martin718Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams719Alexander Albon🇹🇭Williams520Yuki Tsunoda🇯🇵Racing Bulls1Yet to score:Lance Stroll🇨🇦Aston MartinValtteri Bottas🇫🇮CadillacSergio Pérez🇲🇽CadillacConstructors' standings1Mercedes🇩🇪 607pts2Ferrari🇮🇹 4743Red Bull🇦🇹 3554McLaren🇬🇧3555Racing Bulls🇮🇹 1026Alpine🇫🇷 697Haas🇺🇸 308Audi🇩🇪 239Williams🇬🇧1210Aston Martin🇬🇧711Cadillac🇺🇸 0Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Just as his five-race run of victories at the start of the season had given him command of the title fight, he is closing it out with nerveless control. The pole, he admitted, had been something of a surprise given how strong Red Bull have been of late but the victory was an emphatic reminder that these are the performances Antonelli is always capable of delivering.Moreover, the result was welcomed with open arms at Mercedes. The minor wobble they experienced when their upgrades brought to Malaysiadid not deliver as expectedand left the team having to work at bringing the package up to speed, looks to be over. The upgrade is not where they want it to be, the car’s operating window is narrower, but they have a handle on it that the victory demonstrated even if, as Wolff noted, the car remains unsuited to Russell’s style.That is particularly true in comparison to Antonelli, in whose hands the Mercedes once more looked like it was on rails. He went into this race needing to win and he delivered, ensuring that the title race is all over bar the shouting.Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Motor sportFormula OneKimi AntonelliMercedes GPGeorge RussellLewis HamiltonnewsShareReuse this content

title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Alexander Isak was on target again as Liverpool ended Brighton’s four-game winning run in the league with a 2-0 victory at Anfield
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Alexander Isak was on target again as Liverpool ended Brighton’s four-game winning run in the league with a 2-0 victory at Anfield
Content: Alexander Isak is congratulated by teammates after scoring Liverpool’s second goal.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAView image in fullscreenAlexander Isak is congratulated by teammates after scoring Liverpool’s second goal.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAPremier LeagueIsak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an endAndy Hunterat AnfieldSun 25 Oct 2026 12.12 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBrighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in thePremier Leaguethis season, who looked upwardly mobile.There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially creditedto Brighton’s Pascal Grossand Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break.Manchester United 0-3 Bournemouth, Liverpool 2-0 Brighton and more: clockwatch – as it happenedRead moreFabian Hürzeler praised the Brighton performance and the self-belief necessary to take the game toLiverpoolwhen trailing to two quickfire goals. But he exaggerated the threat they displayed. Yasin Ayari missed a glorious chance to open the scoring and also struck a post, but Alisson was troubled more by his own distribution after Liverpool’s second goal than by anything the visitors engineered.“I think everyone in the stadium saw there was one team who really tried to create and tried to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” claimed the Brighton head coach, prompting a mass raising of eyebrows in the post-match press conference. “The difference was that they scored and we didn’t. They blocked a lot of shots and defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes and lost some important personal duels but overall I saw a team with a lot of good things. It is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”Storm Boelo raged outside the stadium but inside it was relatively calm, vindicating the decision to proceed with the game. But not for Brighton. Liverpool’s attacking force devastated the visitors’ hopes of a fifth straight win and clean sheet in succession in the Premier League. The hosts were aggressive and sharp from the start, in contrast to their opening against Villarreal in the Champions League, and opened the scoring just as Brighton were beginning to exert their first serious spell of pressure.There was an element of good fortune about the breakthrough but it also encapsulated the differing intensity between the teams when Wirtz held off Lewis Dunk and Araújo beat the Brighton captain and Olivier Boscagli to the loose ball. His low cross rebounded off two Brighton players before going to Wirtz, whose first-time shot deceived Bart Verbruggen via another deflection off Gross. Wirtz’s low-key celebration hinted at what was to come. It was not his first league goal of the campaign and second goal in successive games after all. The breakthrough was officially credited as an own goal from the Brighton midfielder.View image in fullscreenFlorian Wirtz’s shot was credited as an own goal by his fellow German, Pascal Gross.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAIt should also have been a Liverpool equaliser rather than the opener. Diego Gómez and Gross combined to pierce Liverpool’s left flank and present Ayari with a free sight of goal with Alisson dragged across to his left. The Brighton forward blazed high into the Kop and would soon have added reason to rue the miscue.Liverpool soon doubled their lead when capitalising on more casual Brighton defending. Boscagli was again found wanting when attempting to deal with Alisson’s clearance. The left-back struck a clearance straight at Barcola and was left floundering as the France international, deployed on the right, brushed aside his efforts to recover possession. Isak steered Barcola’s delivery inside the far corner with a deft, side-foot finish to score in three consecutive league games for the first time since January 2025. There was no surprise whatsoever when Boscagli was withdrawn at half-time.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBrighton attacked with greater conviction than they defended but with Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk making telling interventions, and receiving impressive support from all quarters, Alisson was not seriously extended. The visitors’ best hope of a recovery stemmed from the Liverpool keeper’s own risky pass to Alexis Mac Allister, which gifted possession back to Brighton and resulted in Ayari striking a post from 20 yards out.Jack Hinshelwood, Boscagli’s replacement, and fellow substitute Malick Yalcouyé injected more energy and bite into Brighton’s second-half display but an end product from the visitors remained lacking. Too many overhit crosses and poor final balls enabled Liverpool to protect their lead in comfort.Iraola said: “It is a very valuable win. The key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions, and we’ve done it and it has been a different game from the last oneswhen we’ve conceded first.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueLiverpoolBrighton & Hove Albionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Osula and Barnes strike as Newcastle pile pressure on lacklustre Palace | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Newcastle went through the gears at the start of the second half to win 2-0 and increase the sense of gloom around Selhurst Park
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Newcastle went through the gears at the start of the second half to win 2-0 and increase the sense of gloom around Selhurst Park
Content: Newcastle’s second, scored by Harvey Barnes, killed the game as a meaningful contest.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenNewcastle’s second, scored by Harvey Barnes, killed the game as a meaningful contest.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianPremier LeagueOsula and Barnes strike as Newcastle pile pressure on lacklustre PalaceJonathan Wilsonat Selhurst ParkSun 25 Oct 2026 12.29 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe first half was dreadful. The pass completion rate was a meagre 72.8%, although it felt lower. There were only two shots on target. The sun kept popping out from behind the clouds to take a look, and then going back in again, appalled. And the really bad news forCrystal Palaceis that, for them, that was the good bit.Newcastle were much improved after the break. Will Osula touched in a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time, Joe Willock had an effort ruled out for a marginal offside five minutes later, and Harvey Barnes completed a slick passing move six minutes after that. A smattering of boos from the home fans made clear what everybody already knew. Quarter of an hour of proper football had been enough to win the game, and that leaves Pierre Sageunder significant pressure.Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace managerRead moreTo an extent he is a victim of circumstance; a falling tide lowers all boats. The decline at Palace is evident everywhere from the shabby stadiumto the summer sales, Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Muñoz joining the familiar exodus. Two wins in eight league games is troubling, particularly when one of them was as freakish asthe previous home game against Nottingham Forest, when they were outplayed for much of the first half and inexplicably went in ahead at half-time. Nobody could have drawn much confidence from that, andthe shellacking they sustained at Brighton last weekis the kind of thing that might have got a manager more than a few weeks in the job the sack. Patience, though, can only be extended so long.There were a couple of early chances. Daichi Kamada sliced his finish after a promising run by Dwight McNeil. Jean-Philippe Mateta, so devastatingwhen Palace beat Newcastle in April, dragged a shot wide. McNeil rolled a low pass through a vacant six-yard box after good work from Yéremy Pino. But that golden age of incident soon passed.By the quarter-hour an eerie silence had already fallen over Selhurst Park. It was not just that nothing was happening, it was that there was no expectation of anything happening. In part it was the blustery wind on a chilly autumnal afternoon, but there was also the sense that these are two fundamentally ordinary sides, low on confidence, coming to terms with new managers, neither of whom can have a huge amount of confidence that they will still be in their roles in a couple of months.No weather conditions can explain why so many basic passes were misplaced, why the ball spent so much time bouncing aimlessly around the centre circle, or why shots kept being struck into players a couple of feet away.View image in fullscreenPierre Sage has struggled since taking over as Crystal Palace manager from Oliver Glasner.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianAnd that is the other worry for Palace. This was not a defeat against a high-flyer or a team in form. After a mildly promising start to the season, anxiety has begun to set in for Newcastle.They were booed offlast week after losing at home against Aston Villa, their third defeat in four. Losing against an improving Villa in itself is no disgrace; the issue was more the manner of it. Had it worked, the deployment of Dan Burn as an emergency centre‑forward would have been hailed as inspired thinking outside the box; but it did not work – and, really, how likely was it to? – and so it looked like desperation.The appeals for patience are reasonable enough: Matthias Jaissle has been in charge for only three months and replacing a manager whohad been in charge for five yearsis rarely a straightforward process, even if the squad has not lost its three best players. But at the same time £260m was spent on eight signings, of whom only Nico González has made much of an impact so far, although Amar Dedic was solid enough here.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBurn, restored to the back four alongside Fabian Schär ahead of Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw, was immense, untroubled by the physicality of Mateta, of whom it may charitably be said that he is not back to his best after injury. The defence generally looked assured, while González was pretty much the only player in that chaotic first half who had any sense that some semblance of shape may be desirable. This is a squad still taking shape, with the new signings presumably to be introduced gradually but, ultimately, Newcastle should be comfortably mid-table.It’s hard to have such confidence in Palace. Lukas Hornicek did have to make two saves around the midpoint of the second half, first from an Adam Wharton curler and then a long-range drive from Darío Osorio, but there was very little threat, very little imagination and very little quality from them.Newcastle were far from brilliant, but that 15-minute spell after half‑time was more than enough for them to win the game comfortably. There is discontent at Palace, and it is justified.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueCrystal PalaceNewcastle Unitedmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Marcus Smith produces timely reminder of his class as Harlequins sink Saracens | Prem Rugby | The Guardian
description: Marcus Smith starred for Harlequins in their 33-15 derby victory against Saracens
Author: Luke McLaughlin
Headline: Marcus Smith starred for Harlequins in their 33-15 derby victory against Saracens
Content: Marcus Smith carries the fight to Saracens during Harlequins’ home win.Photograph: Andrew Fosker/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenMarcus Smith carries the fight to Saracens during Harlequins’ home win.Photograph: Andrew Fosker/ShutterstockPrem RugbyMarcus Smith produces timely reminder of his class as Harlequins sink SaracensHarlequins 33-15 SaracensEngland fly-half marks 200th appearance in styleLuke McLaughlinat the Twickenham StoopSun 25 Oct 2026 13.30 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMarcus Smith celebrated his 200th Harlequins match in magnificent style. Perhaps there is a danger, at times, of taking his immense talent for granted, but he was unstoppable here. A powerful visiting Saracens side barely got a look-in, with Smith reminding us all of his ability on the daySteve Borthwick named his England squadfor a packed November.Smith’s sensational running, distribution and tactical kicking masterfully controlled Quins’ attack for a badly needed success. They were nought from three in the league and this was a vital result for reasons more important than Smith’s personal prestige.Joe Marchant recalled to England training squad for Nations ChampionshipRead moreDefensive discipline and forward muscle was as significant as the customary soft hands and creative vision. It is only one victory but the storm clouds gathering around Jason Gilmore, the head coach – and the rest of the club’s hierarchy – have cleared to some extent.Gilmore paid tribute to Smith: “The work he puts in, the way he cares about the club, he’s only 27 and played 200 games for us. We’re so lucky to have him. He led us around the park and I’m really proud of Smithy.”Saracens – despite the presence of Maro Itoje, George Martin and Ben Earl – struggled to make an impact, hardly helped by their indiscipline; Earl and Fergus Burke were shown yellow cards before half-time.Brendan Venter’s rotation policy may begin to raise eyebrows: Noah Caluori, Owen Farrell and Charlie Bracken were doing shuttle runs 10 minutes before kick-off. There are not many clubs who would ignore players of that quality as a matter of course.“We have chopped and changed, so I understand why people are asking that,” Joe Shaw, the Saracens head coach, said of his side’s obvious lack of cohesion. “It’s not some random thing we’re trying to be quirky with. We believe there is merit in what we’re doing.”The Prem weekend had been characterised by stormy weather and old-fashioned wrestlesat Welford Roadand Ashton Gate, in conditions that did not favour free‑flowing rugby.A stiff breeze remained but the appearance of the sun played into Quins’ hands. Smith proved the point within three minutes, launching an attack down the left before capitalising on slick handling from George Furbank and Cadan Murley to sprint over. The crowd were on their feet. The tone was set.The prop Fin Baxter, returning from a 10-month injury layoff, soon demonstrated Quins are about more than silky skill, producing a muscular carry in the 22 before a delightful one‑handed offload for the openside Seb Driscoll, who smashed through the Sarries No 9, Tomos Williams, and over the line.The wing Rotimi Segun did get Saracens on the board with a fine twisting finish after the visitors worked through the phases into the Quins’ 22, with Martin, Rhys Carré and Theo Dan making inroads before Williams’s looping pass to the left.But Quins, as if to prove a point, soon went to the driving maul at the other end, culminating in a penalty try and Earl in the sin bin for collapsing it.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSmith’s afternoon got better when Max Malins was sent cantering over the line on 26 minutes thanks to more sharp work by Segun. The England back, hungry to make a difference at both ends, chased a seemingly lost cause and batted the ball out of Malins’s hands.Saracens’ media strategyhas been debated recentlyand a three-word message on social media last week – “Their cup final” – raised the pre-match temperature. Rather like Northampton’s Henry Pollock and his embarrassing involvement in a scuffle at Leicester on Saturday – that only served to motivate the opposition – it was a provocative move from Saracens that seemed to backfire. Before half-time, Burke was shown a yellow card for an upright tackle on Rodrigo Isgró before Murley pounced for Quins’ fourth: bonus point secured, 26-5 at half-time. Saracens had missed 22 tackles and conceded 10 penalties.On 55 minutes Quins twisted the knife. Williams flung a long pass out for Segun on the Saracens left where he knocked it on: Will Porter, the No 9, kicked ahead, collected and took advantage of some halfhearted defending to score Quins’ fifth and final try. It was a ragged effort from Sarries and will be a horrible one for their post-match analysis.Tottenham’s 2-0 win against Chelsea on Saturday– another significant London derby – was distinctly un‑Spursy. Here was a heartening, notably un‑Quinsy, victory for Smith, the player of the match, and his suddenly resurgent team.“He’s brilliant isn’t he?” Shaw said of Smith, adding the derby defeat left him with an “awful feeling”.“We planned for him not to be that brilliant. He can pick you off. It’s a disappointing day at the office.”Explore more on these topicsPrem RugbyHarlequinsSaracensRugby unionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: England stunned after Shadab Khan’s miraculous century delivers one-wicket win for Pakistan | Cricket | The Guardian
description: Shadab Khan made an unbeaten 113 in a thrilling last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf as Pakistan, chasing 242, beat England in a thriller
Author: Tanya Aldred
Headline: Shadab Khan made an unbeaten 113 in a thrilling last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf as Pakistan, chasing 242, beat England in a thriller
Content: Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf roar in delight after Pakistan’s fightback against England.Photograph: KM Chaudary/APView image in fullscreenShadab Khan and Haris Rauf roar in delight after Pakistan’s fightback against England.Photograph: KM Chaudary/APCricketEngland stunned after Shadab Khan’s miraculous century delivers one-wicket win for PakistanEngland blow victory chance after hosts were 154 for nineShadab makes unbeaten 113 in thrillerTanya AldredSun 25 Oct 2026 12.49 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 15.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleShadab Khan whipped the rug from under England’s boots with an ­eye-popping 113, a blitz of boundary peppering when hope was lost, the one-wicket win guaranteeing Pakistan a place in the tri-series final. England,for the second time in four days, watched a sure thing swirl down the drain.With Pakistan 154 for nine in their run chase, 88 away from victory, queues were beginning to build at the Gaddafi Stadium exits. But Shadab had other ideas, and with No 11 Haris Rauf providing adhesive company, went on the rampage. Balls disappeared over this boundary and that as England giggled nervously into their hands. The drama doubled when Shadab was given out lbw on 97, slamming his bat into the turf in frustration, hands shaken with England, before an inside edge was discovered on a what-the-heck review.Pakistan beat England in thriller after 89-run last-wicket stand: tri-series one day international cricket – liveRead moreFrom there 21 were needed, and 21 were hit, nail-nibbling minutes encompassing Rauf arguing a Sam Curran wide with Will Jacks having to be placated by Joe Root, a first ­hundred in any international cricket for Shadab, and Rauf driving Henry Crocombe for four to win the game by one wicket. Their partnership of 89 was the highest for the 10th wicket in any successful ODI chase.After the cut-throat chubbiness of Thursday’s 859-run glut, this was pared-down cricket. Pakistan, in West Indies World Series salmon pink for breast cancer, had looked in command at the halfway stage, after England left runs in the middle, all out with 20 balls to spare for just 241. But England’s bowlers kept their nerve and Pakistan’s batters faltered, until Shadab and Rauf’s last stand.Pakistan’s chase started under a purple Lahore night sky, with the ground filling up late. Like England earlier in the day, Pakistan had a tricky power play.A frustrated Fakhar Zaman flashed a drive straight into the giant paws of Jamie Overton at slip in the fifth over to give the immaculate Gus Atkinson his first wicket.The debutant Crocombe, all baggy shirt and rosy cheeks, coltish arms and legs working overtime, shared the new ball. He was on the money with his first over, and a more erratic nine-ball third finished with the wicket of Saim Ayub, who ladled the ball straight to Overton as Crocombe was mobbed. The crowd had one name on its lips and Babar Azam, at his home ground, made them sing with a pure off-drive matched by something equally majestic on the on-side. But just as the glory hit the veins, Atkinson whistled through the gate, firing the top of off, wagging his finger in celebration.Saad Baig picked up the pace with an otherworldly 32, until a bullet was collected by Jacks at backward point off Overton, who had pulled up in his delivery stride earlier in the over.View image in fullscreenBen Duckett ended up on the losing side despite completing his fifth ODI century.Photograph: Rahat Dar/EPAFrom there, it was cat and mouse: could England frustrate Pakistan into giving wickets away? Yes they could, as Liam Dawson and Overton bowled on a button, and finally Hasan Nawaz yahooed Dawson into the stratosphere, Harry Brook waiting for his prize. Arafat Minhas lasted just three balls before directing Overton to Root, who had just been ushered to short fine leg by Brook.Salman Ali Agha had a meaty slog at Dawson, Razaullah, also on ODI debut, got a gorgeous ball from Jacks between bat and pad to leave Pakistan nine down. It looked like game over.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionEarlier, Ben Duckett’s fifth ODI century was the backbone of an ­England innings that sparked in places but was blotted by clusters of wickets. His second century at Lahore was dominated by sweeps of various hues, but after Pakistan won the toss and bowled, England’s first four wickets lined up like a pin number: 4, 5, 1, 6.Tom Banton clipped the superb Shaheen Shah Afridi’s fifth ball to cover to give him a 150th ODI wicket. Root had time, just, to dispatch Afridi to the boundary before leaning back and enveloping him to point.Brook, fresh from 202 against Sri Lanka, was undone coming back for a second, fractionally too slow for an inspired Razaullah pick up and throw. Then Jordan Cox tried to nuzzle Rauf to third man but was met by Babar diving to his right at slip.In Curran, Duckett at last found sticking power, and the pair added 93 until Shaheen brought himself back on and Curran took on his shorter ball. As the black kites circled above, England’s last five wickets added 96, Duckett celebrating his first hundred against Pakistan with a low-key kiss of the badge, but they looked underdone and so it proved. To reach the final, England need Pakistan to beat Sri Lanka on Tuesday before thrashing Sri Lanka on Thursday.Explore more on these topicsCricketEngland cricket teamPakistan cricket teammatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller  | La Liga | The Guardian
description: The French forward scored in the 41st and 87th minute as Real Madrid closed the gap on the La Liga leaders Barcelona with a 2-1 win
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: The French forward scored in the 41st and 87th minute as Real Madrid closed the gap on the La Liga leaders Barcelona with a 2-1 win
Content: Kylian Mbappé is all smiles after scoring Real Madrid’s 87th-minute winner.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersView image in fullscreenKylian Mbappé is all smiles after scoring Real Madrid’s 87th-minute winner.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersLa LigaMbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha levellerSid Loweat the Camp NouSun 25 Oct 2026 18.12 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 19.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThirteen years later, José Mourinho ledReal Madridinto the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written.“The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again.Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: El Clásico – live reactionRead moreIn the corner, Madrid’s players piled on. This was the Frenchman’s 10th goal against Barcelona butnone felt quite like this. Not only was this the first time Barcelona failed to win in the league this season, their record-equalling run halted at nine; it was the first time they had failed to win any game since returning here a year ago.“I’m not going to let them have their heads on the moon,” Mourinho said, but he knew what this meant. So much for a struggling side heading to an inevitable fall; so much forBarcelonagoing nine points clear, the title race run before November. There is life in Madrid and in this league. Life in their manager too: this was expertly planned and executed, the rivals who were running at 4.3 goals per game reduced to just one. Those certainties, misplaced, seemed a long way away now; a season starts here instead.In the beginning, the ball was all Barcelona’s but no sooner had they lost it than the first shot was Madrid’s, Pedri’s startlingly loose pass allowing Arda Guler to break and fire over on four minutes. That felt like a pattern set, a portrait of the way both teams would likely approach this. So too did the way that Marc Cucurella went for Lamine Yamal, the Madrid full-back seeking a way under the winger’s skin – a task in which, it had to be ­concluded, he was successful.View image in fullscreenRaphinha is congratulated by his teammates after scoring Barcelona’s equaliser.Photograph: Jose Breton/APThe impression though was deceptive, Madrid willing to step on to the front foot and apply a pressure with which Barcelona were not comfortable, Pedri and Rodri unable to fully settle. Where they could they played too, Bernardo Silva included alongside Aurélien Tchouaméni.They were also, naturally enough, ready to run. In those early phases, Fede Valverde was opening the pitch with long diagonals. From one, Mbappé went dashing up the left, leading to Joan García scooping away ­Guler’s shot. This was frantic and Madrid were finding it to their liking, Mbappé and Yan Diomandé a threat.Quick GuideEuropean football roundupShowBallon d’Or contender Harry Kane failed to find the net on Sunday, butBayernMunichwon 3-1 away atFreiburgto regain top spot in the Bundesliga.The visitors took a 2-0 lead through Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry — his 100th goal in the Bundesliga — before an 82nd-minute Tom Bischof own goal brought Freiburg back into the contest, but Michael Olise secured victory for Bayern in the fifth minute of added time.Bayern remain without their head coach, Vincent Kompany, who collapsed during training on Friday, but lead the Bundesliga on goal difference fromBorussia Dortmund, who beatEintracht Frankfurt1-0 on Saturday.Marcus Thuram scored and then earned the penalty  that decidedInter’s late, come-from-behind 2-1 victory over visitingFiorentina.Álex Jiménez had put Fiorentina ahead midway through the second half at San Siro. Thuram equalised in the first minute of added time with a low shot through traffic and  was tugged down minutes later to set up a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the seventh minute of stoppage time.That late comeback  moved Inter back to the top of the table, level on 22 points with Lazio but ahead on goal difference.Juventuseased pastLeccein Serie A, with first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz enough to secure a 2-0 victory.It was only Juve's second win in six league outings, an inconsistent run of early season form that sees Luciano Spalletti's just outside the European places in Italy.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The hosts tried to impose control but could not. That said, they too enjoy flying into space, and from a Pedri run Raphinha shot over. Then Anthony Gordon bombed through and produced a neat back-heel for Raphinha to curl wide. The Brazilian would have another shot wide soon after, although the openings were often lost to an insistence on playing (and ­wasting) one last pass or, conversely, to snatch at shots. The half’s best opportunity came when Guler’s gorgeous ball was volleyed over by Mbappé. Back and forth it went, Gordon drawing a sharp save from Andriy Lunin.In the midst of it all the Camp Nou roared in indignation with each, increasingly intense Cucurella challenge on Lamine Yamal, before silence fell on 41 minutes. Cucurella released Diomandé, so often the destination, who pulled across low and hard. Gerard Martín got there first but could only hit it against Mbappé and in. There was fortune there, but it had been worked for, not simply found. And when Lamine Yamal had a wonderful chance to level he wasted the opportunity, scuffing wide at the near post, a picture of a night that wasn’t his.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOlder, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásicoRead moreBarcelona came back at Madrid in the second half. The tackles around the box were racking up: Tchouaméni and Bellingham, Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté. The threat never went away, Martín ended one ­Bellingham break, but the match had tilted. On the hour Barcelona were level. Lamine Yamal took a corner short to Pedri who slipped a clever angled, reversed ball into Raphinha to strike low into the net.The noise rose. Raphinha was denied at one end. García saved from Guler at the other. And, Barcelona back again, Lunin made an astonishing stop from Martín’s header. Barcelona had taken a grip but not entirely, leaving them exposed to every break and leaving the game, the players and the entire place on edge. Mbappé ran at Barcelona, Pedri ran back again, leading a move that concluded with some neat footwork and a shot just wide. Huijsen then dived in to stop Frenkie de Jong and stopped a Lamine Yamal shot with his face, laying him out. The chance had been laid on by Gordon.Barcelona insisted. Madrid, tired now, resisted. But there was still some fight in them, and still some finish too.Explore more on these topicsLa LigaBarcelonaReal MadridEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Manchester United’s Elisabeth Terland struck an 89th-minute equaliser to cancel out Khadija Shaw’s goal and earn a 1-1 draw against Manchester City
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Manchester United’s Elisabeth Terland struck an 89th-minute equaliser to cancel out Khadija Shaw’s goal and earn a 1-1 draw against Manchester City
Content: Elisabeth Terland thrashes home the loose ball to secure a point for Manchester United against their city rivals.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenElisabeth Terland thrashes home the loose ball to secure a point for Manchester United against their city rivals.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersWomen's Super LeagueTerland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSLTom Garryat the Progress With Unity StadiumSun 25 Oct 2026 16.38 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 19.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby.Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher.Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSLRead moreHowever, Eva Olid’s ever-improving hosts fought back and were good value for the draw, which they eventually earned when Terland found the bottom corner after the ball fell kindly to her in the penalty area.Olid, in fact, repeatedly said in her post-match press conference that her side had “deserved to win”.United climbed to fourth in the table, while that late strike meant City dropped to ­second – now behind Chelsea on goal difference – and breathed fresh life and intrigue into the title race. Perhaps more strikingly, if any United fans who saw their men’s team beinghumbled by Bournemouthearlier on Sunday managed to navigate the winds of Storm Boelo and get to Leigh for this 6pm kick-off, they will have seen a team with characteristics unrecognisable from those wearing red at Old Trafford; hard work, resilience, teamwork, running – real, hard running – and fighting spirit.This United team markedly improved on last season’s league meetings with their local rivals, both of which ended in 3-0 victories for City. This time Andrée Jeglertz’s visitors were given a real test.Quick GuideWSL roundup:ShowChelseacame from behind to beatCrystal Palace3-1 after Molly Bartrip’s shock opener. It was the first time Chelsea had trailed all season and they struck back in the second half with two Melvine Malard goals, before Sandy Baltimore converted from the penalty spot in the 90th minute.London City Lionessesstayed third after drawing 2-2 atLiverpool, with the visitors denied all three points by a stoppage-time own goal from Jana Fernández. Freya Godfrey and Kadidiatou Diani had earlier wiped out Beata Olsson’s penalty.Aston Villamoved level on points withEvertonafter winning 3-2 at Goodison Park. Amalie Vangsgaard’s double put Villa three up after Noelle Maritz’s early goal, before the hosts made it a nervy finish with two late goals.Birminghamwon for the first time this season as Wilma Leidhammar’s effort midway through the second half saw offCharlton1-0.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.For spells of the first half, City’s fluid pass-and-move football, their speed down the left-wing with ­Lauren Hemp, and the technical prowess of Yui Hasegawa and Aoba Fujino in particular, made it feel as though there was only one likely outcome, as Fujino fizzed an effort narrowly wide of the United goal.United, though, proved a tough nut to crack and, against the run of play, created the better chances of the opening 45 minutes.Terland was unable to reset her feet and ­connect properly with Andrea Medina’s ­cutback. Later Ella Toone and Jess Park both had efforts saved by Ayaka Yamashita.View image in fullscreenKhadija Shaw blasts Manchester City into the lead against United.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersPark’s powerful, driven shot clipped the top of the crossbar around the hour mark, after Yamashita had saved well from Terland one-on-one.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNot long later, though, last season’s WSL Golden Boot winner Shaw ­delivered the breakthrough with a ruthless, low strike that was hit with too much venom for Phallon ­Tullis-Joyce to react. Shaw, who had been booed by the home fans after exchanging robust challenges with Maya Le Tissier in the first half, ran across to celebrate in front of the City fans, many of whom were waving inflatable bananas in the air. She almost had a second goal moments later but whipped a close-range, rising shot just over the bar.Shaw glanced a header wide from a City corner and Grace Clinton missed a huge chance to seal it for the ­visitors. Continuing to battle, United were eventually rewarded when Le Tissier’s hopeful, high ball into the box, after a free-kick was taken short, was met by a defensive header from Shaw, but that only dropped as far as Terland who lashed in first time to draw huge roars and clenched fists from the United technical area.Jeglertz is staying calm, insisting: “Nothing has changed. We are absolutely on the right track, in everything we are doing. We are playing well in most of the games and getting the result in most of the games. But this league is challenging. [We are just going] to stay calm and focusing on the next task.”As for United, this late goal felt like a pivotal moment for Olid, giving the club a lift. Her tenure began with chastening losses to London City and Chelsea but this rally against their neighbours showed they are rapidly improving. She said: “That was one of our best performances, in general, in terms of fight, hard work, how we were ­pressing and how we played with the ball.“How this team has built in confidence from day one to now, in a short period of time – just two months and a half working together – the progression has been massive.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueManchester United WomenManchester City WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘If it was up to me it wouldn’t end like this’: Jimmy Anderson confirms Lancashire exit | Jimmy Anderson | The Guardian
description: Jimmy Anderson has expressed regret at how his 25-year spell with Lancashire has come to an end after the club confirmed he will not be offered a new contract
Author: Daniel Gallan
Headline: Jimmy Anderson has expressed regret at how his 25-year spell with Lancashire has come to an end after the club confirmed he will not be offered a new contract
Content: James Anderson in his last Test, against West Indies at Lord’s, in July 2024.Photograph: Graham Hunt/ProSports/REX/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenJames Anderson in his last Test, against West Indies at Lord’s, in July 2024.Photograph: Graham Hunt/ProSports/REX/ShutterstockJimmy Anderson‘If it was up to me it wouldn’t end like this’: Jimmy Anderson confirms Lancashire exitEngland’s all-time record wicket-taker not offered new contractBowler has spent 25 years at countyDaniel GallanSun 25 Oct 2026 08.04 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 12.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJimmy Anderson has confirmed he will leave Lancashire when his contract ends this year, after the county decided not to extend his deal for the 2027 season. The 44-year-old has not said whether he will retire or continue playing elsewhere.Anderson reflected on hisLancashirecareer on Instagram. “I’ve supported Lancashire since I was a kid, and so to get to play for them for 25 years was a dream come true,” he wrote. “I have always found it special walking out to play at Old Trafford and have some incredible memories of doing so, including the honour of being captain.Bavuma’s nine-hour masterpiece was art we risk losing in Test cricket’s great purge | Barney RonayRead more“If it was up to me it wouldn’t have ended like this, but I wish the players and fans all the best for the future.”Anderson made his Lancashire debut in 2001. He took 443 first-class wickets for the county in 112 appearances, plus 83 List A wickets in 61 matches and 50 T20 wickets in 40 appearances. His 50 wickets in the 2026 Championship at an average of 17.68 earned him Lancashire’s Championship player of the year award. The county finished second-bottom in Division Two and exited both limited-overs competitions in the group stage.Paul Farbrace, Lancashire’s incoming director of cricket, said he had told Anderson the club would not extend his contract after a meeting with the chief executive, Richard Kenyon, on 19 October. Farbrace said the club wanted to rebuild its squad to secure promotion and then challenge in Division One over the next three to four years. “LancashireCricketcan confirm that, following a remarkable 25-year association with the Red Rose, Sir James Anderson’s playing career with the club will come to an end at the conclusion of his current contract,” read a statement from the county.The former England captain Nasser Hussain said Anderson’s departure was “a hugely sad way” for the bowler to leave the club. “I’d say most counties in the country would take Anderson, even at the age of 44,” he wrote for Sky Sports. “I’d rather not focus in on how it ended, both for England and for Lancashire – I’d rather be thankful that we’ve had 26 years of Anderson giving it all for England and Lancashire.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAnderson’s Lancashire exit follows hisretirement from international cricketin July 2024. Anderson’s 188th and final Test was against West Indies at Lord’s. He finished his Test career with 704 wickets, the most by any fast bowler.Explore more on these topicsJimmy AndersonLancashireCounty ChampionshipCricketShareReuse this content

title: Former Tory candidate suspended over contract killer claims was adviser in Kemi Badenoch’s office | Conservatives | The Guardian
description: Sources close to Tory leader say Jack Ross, who faces party investigation after undercover report, worked as social media consultant
Author: Ben Quinn
Headline: Sources close to Tory leader say Jack Ross, who faces party investigation after undercover report, worked as social media consultant
Content: Jack Ross, a former Tory local election candidate and CEO of Turning Point UK, was filmed by an undercover reporter discussing the cost of hiring hitmen.Photograph: Guy Corbishley/AlamyView image in fullscreenJack Ross, a former Tory local election candidate and CEO of Turning Point UK, was filmed by an undercover reporter discussing the cost of hiring hitmen.Photograph: Guy Corbishley/AlamyConservativesFormer Tory candidate suspended over contract killer claims was adviser in Kemi Badenoch’s officeSources close to Tory leader say Jack Ross, who faces party investigation after undercover report, worked as social media consultantBen QuinnandJessica ElgotSun 25 Oct 2026 09.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 13.15 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA former Conservative election candidate who was suspended after he was filmed discussing the cost of hiring contract killers worked as a consultant in Kemi Badenoch’s office as recently as last year.Jack Ross is facing an investigation by the Tories after he was filmed apparently asking an undercover reporter: “What do you want done?” and apparently offering to “broker” the services of an alleged far-right paramilitary group.Police in Scotland say they will be reviewing an Al Jazeera documentary in which Ross was filmed making a range comments about what a contract killer could be employed to do, and talked about using far-right groups to create disruption on the streets.It has now emerged that he was working in 2025 in the leader of the opposition’s office, which can draw on taxpayer funds to pay staff. By that point, Ross was CEO of Turning Point UK, which was already involving itself in anti-migrant street protests, and listed its chief operating officer as Nick Tenconi, the leader of Ukip.Sources close to Badenoch said Ross was contracted as a junior social media external consultant in her office. However, a Tory staffer familiar with the role of Ross at that time said: “Jack would come and go in the office and a few people raised their eyebrows, but it was brushed under the carpet because he got the party clicks on socials.“He would have been in the same room as Kemi and she would have been aware of him. Some MPs were uncomfortable about it, but senior figures were clear that social media clicks were more important.”Ross wasreported by Al Jazeerato have introduced an undercover reporter to a violent criminal from Glasgow with links to the paramilitary Ulster Volunteer Force, who offered to have people killed for money.Al Jazeera approached Ross with a fictitious family problem where a deceased uncle’s business was at risk of being taken over by a gang, whose members were supposedly warned they would “get fucked” if anything happened.Ross replied to this saying: “Yeah, you have to deliver on that as well. You’ve got to explain to me what’s needed … I can then go and broker from there. But I’ve got to say, even to myself … if there’s lashback I’ve got to keep my name out of it.”On another occasion, Ross was filmed apparently asking an undercover reporter “What do you want done?” before listing the type of violent options that could be bought.Ross appeared to tell the Al Jazeera journalist: “They can just kick the fuck out of someone. That’s a certain amount. They can start cutting people’s faces up, that’s another amount. And they can stab someone. They can shoot someone. They can kill someone.”Ross, who stood unsuccessfully as a Conservative local election candidate, became CEO of Turning Point UK (TPUK) in 2021, the British offshoot of the US campaign group established by the late rightwing American activist Charlie Kirk. Ross became a fixture of the British rightwing scene, appearing regularly on GB News and joining the conservative thinktank the Bow Group.TPUK was intended to be a campus-based offshoot of the US group and initially endorsed by leading Tory figures such as Priti Patel and Jacob Rees-Mogg. Early members included younger rightwingers such as Tom Harwood, who went on to become a GB News anchor.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFirst EditionOur morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it mattersEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHowever, it began reinventing itself as a street-protest group after the addition of Tenconi, who has worked closely with Ross, as its COO. Tenconi, as leader of Ukip, has been at the forefont of leading immigration protests in recent years, blending anti-migrant rhetoric with Christian nationalism.Footage released by TPUK last year showed Ross and others from the group meeting Badenoch after Kirk’s deathTPUK has not responded to the allegations but Tenconi staged a stunt outside King’s College London on Thursday in an imitation of the campus-based events held by Kirk. A gazebo with TPUK branding was surrounded by students and protesters chanting in opposition.Al Jazeera filmed Tenconi in the company of Ross in 2022 as they discussed the formation of a “new right” which would include the engagement of far-right activists who could cause disruption on the streets, as well as what Tenconi described as the “winning over” of sympathetic MPs.A Tory spokesperson said: “Mr Ross’s membership of the Conservative party has been suspended with immediate effect pending an investigation. We cannot comment further while the investigation is ongoing.”Ross and Tenconi have been approached for comment.Explore more on these topicsConservativesKemi BadenochThe far rightnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron Cohen | Movies | The Guardian
description:
Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’

• This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?
Author: Catherine Shoard
Headline: Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’• This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?
Content: ‘I was a little offended. You’re picking on these Americans that aren’t the brightest’ … Loudermilk in the trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I?Photograph: Ali G: Who Iz I?View image in fullscreen‘I was a little offended. You’re picking on these Americans that aren’t the brightest’ … Loudermilk in the trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I?Photograph: Ali G: Who Iz I?Movies‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron CohenExclusive:Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?Catherine ShoardSun 25 Oct 2026 12.13 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 12.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJoshua Loudermilk, one of two men apparently discredited by the new Ali G movieAli G: Who Iz I?, has said that he was in on the joke, but that the film-makers didn’t realise this.Loudermilk, a 54-year-old aspiring actor from North Carolina, has told the Guardian he recognised starSacha Baron Cohenearly in the shoot but continued pretending to be a hard-right Maga sympathiser prepared to defend the US border at all costs.The movie involves Loudermilk being recruited by another Cohen character, the ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad, to help form a citizens’ warrior force to protect US borders, making use of his top-secret new weapon: a gun disguised as buttocks.Along with fellow recruit Michael Aboud, the chair of the El Paso county Republican party, Loudermilk joins Morad on a mission to stop the birth on US soil of the baby of a fictional South American drugs kinpin. This involves abducting a woman apparently in labour, abandoning her in a deserted medical facility, kidnapping her newborn child (a lifelike prosthetic) and driving it in a zipped bag to the border in order to deliver it by drone to Mexico.Republican leader embarrassed by Ali G film says he plans to sue Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘A liar and a pervert’Read moreAboud is shown taking the decision to drop the child from a great height into Mexico rather than have it touch US soil. He has since called Cohen a “liar” and a “pervert” and expressed his intention to sue. The film repeatedly stresses that both men were “not in on it”.Loudermilk has told the Guardian he was surprised the production company did not notice social media updates he posted shortly after the shoot in which he named Cohen and expressed his excitement about the project.But rather than being upset about his involvement, Loudermilk – who recently appeared as Squire Dap in the North Carolina Town of Hudson Fall Dinner Theatre’s production of Camelot – says he welcomes the publicity boost.“I want to use this to my benefit,” he says. “I would hope Sacha would read this and laugh, like: ‘Hey, you got me!’ I had so much fun creating that character. I was trying to see if I was any good at acting in comedy. And I realised: ‘Oh, I think I’m good at this.’ And that’s what I wanna do for the rest of my life.”View image in fullscreenJoshua Loudermilk.Photograph: Joshua LoudermilkHis experience began in September 2025 when Loudermilk spotted apost on Craigslistby a body called the American Citizen Initiative (whose website is no longer active) recruiting “patriotic legal Americans” “concerned about the border crisis” who “believe that illegal immigration is out of control”.The ad, one of dozens posted across US states simultaneously, invited “real American citizens” to “attend an exclusive, hands-on event experience where you’ll learn the truth about what’s happening on the border and how you can make a difference”. Attendees were promised $300 as well as travel expenses.“I was like: this seems kind of weird,” says Loudermilk, who describes himself as broadly apolitical. “I don’t really care much about our borders. My mom’s from Ireland.”Recently made redundant, his motivation for responding was primarily financial. “I know rightwing and leftwing organisations have money and will pay people to just hold a sign up. I remember thinking: I wanna get on that gravy train. I want some George Soros money. I’ll pretend to be whatever. Just let me feed my family. It could have been save the whales and I would have done it.”In his application, Loudermilk fabricated hard-right views, mentioned that he had been a preacher and neglected to declare his ambitions to become a comedy actor – in part, he says, out of embarrassment. He then filled in a “silly questionnaire – very obvious, very slanted to the right”.Loudermilk was then called for a video interview, which involved the identification of left-leaning celebrities, as well as figures including Borat, Cohen’s bumbling Kazakh reporter, who Loudermilk duly named.He was also asked if he was a Trump supporter. “The funny thing is: not really. He’s just a leader. But I was like: I’m going to be an improv actor so I said: ‘Yeah, I support Trump!’ Next thing I know they’re like, ‘We want you to come out to be a part of this.’The company flew him to Ontario, California, with an initial offer of $1,000, plus food and expenses, on top of which Loudermilk received a further $700. “It was all real secretive. They frisked me down and I got in a truck to go to a karate studio.”Once he arrived, Loudermilk was greeted by security and informed an Israeli commander wanted to meet him. “That was a red flag. Why would Israeli commander be in America? I go in there and immediately I see this really tall guy with this horrible plastic surgery. My first thought was: that looks like Sacha Cohen. But I was like: nah, that can’t be him.”View image in fullscreenSacha Baron Cohen as ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad in the 2018 show Who is America?Photograph: ShowtimeLoudermilk’s suspicions were further raised, he says, when he met his fellow recruits. “They were old, old, old white guys who were really out of shape. Everyone’s wearing these Trump shirts. They didn’t seem like warriors. I thought: they could probably get better people for this.”Morad then produced the top-secret new gun in the shape of large, strap-on bottom, out of which bullets are fired from the anus. Initially, Loudermilk was baffled by its logistics. “I kept thinking: no-one’s gonna wear that thing because your butt’s gonna be abnormally large. No one has a butt like that. Are you gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that. And you’d have to wear some really big khaki pants.”He volunteered to be first to try the weapon out, whereupon Morad demonstrated the trigger system, which involves the pumping of an attached rubber penis. “And he kept calling it ‘shmeckel’. I’m like: that’s Sacha Cohen. At that moment I knew it.“And I was like: oh no, I can’t break character. I’ve got to go along with it. So what I decided [was] that whatever he did, I was going to take it another step further. He’s not going to punk me; I’m going to trick him. So I decided to get into character and just have a good time because they’re paying me.”As the plot became more “ridiculous”, says Loudermilk, so his enjoyment increased. During a scene in which he, Morad and Aboud help deliver the (prosthetic) baby, the three men become covered with fake excrement. “This big blast of pooping pap,” recalls Loudermilk – but he was reassured after inadvertently sampling some of the fluids. “I thought: ‘This doesn’t taste bad.’ So I just kind of hung in there. It was disgusting, but I was having fun.”View image in fullscreenLoudermilk and Aboud in Ali G: Who Iz I?Photograph: Ali G: Who Iz I?At the climax at the Mexican border, says Loudermilk, he handed the remote control to the drone to Aboud, “because that was boring. It was ridiculous – they’re not flying a real baby”. Instead, he “wanted to have fun with Sacha,” so he grabbed the “butt-gun”, yelling about the need to defend themselves, and eventually discharged fire, aided by Morad, who helps pump the penis trigger.Loudermilk declines to defend Aboud’s decision to then endanger the life of the baby by dropping it from the drone, but expresses some sympathy for his unwitting co-star.“I felt sorry for the poor fella. Because I’m all-in and he’s just kind of following me around like in a daze, like: what’s happening? He was scared to death, and obviously very uncomfortable, bless his heart.“I’d never met the guy before, but [at times] it felt he was totally freaking out on me. So I had to make him believe that I believed all this. So I would tell him, ‘You’re being a wimp, man. Our freedom is on the line.’ I kept trying to keep him from quitting.“But I’m surprised he didn’t figure it out. Like, come on, Michael – why would they recruit you to defend our border? Think about it.”Loudermilk concedes his decision to maintain the pretence of being far-right once he had worked out the true nature of the project was in part because he “was a little offended. Like: really? You’re picking on these Americans that aren’t the brightest. You’re gonna make fun of them and they’re not gonna know any better. So I decided I needed to be their ally, even though I’m not that way.”View image in fullscreenBaron Cohen at the film’s Los Angeles premiere.Photograph: Mario Anzuoni/ReutersAt the end of filming, Loudermilk signed a non-disclosure agreement at the request of the production company, which he says he was not given a copy of, and which mostly related to the top-secret weapons. “They came up to me after I was done and said, ‘Oh, you did so well!’ I said, ‘You get what you need? Can I talk about it?’ They said, ‘Oh no, not yet. Especially the butt-gun.’”Loudermilk considers any such terms breached now the film is out and mentions him by name: “It’s fair game.” He adds that, after shooting, he had some qualms about not coming clean to them that he had twigged. “I felt a little bad. And that’s why I thought: I should make a little post.”In December last year, Loudermilk posted three times on his public Facebook page about “eight hours of intense filming one on one with Sasha [sic] Cohen”, as well as twice on his Instagram, which is also public.“But they never saw it. And the fact they missed that makes it even better to me. So I guess it’s on them.”Last week, representatives for the film confirmed again to the Guardian that Loudermilk was not in on the joke. They have not yet responded to a further followup question on this.The film was released nationwide in the UK on Friday, as well as in a limited run in the US. Loudermilk, who has not yet watched it, says he is unconcerned about the prospect of recriminations from anyone upset by his apparent actions.“That people would be disgusted is a compliment. Oh, I really did a good job, huh! I pulled it off and I was so proud of myself.”Explore more on these topicsFilmAli G: Who Iz IRepublicansSacha Baron CohenFilm industryComedy filmsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Ethnic minorities in England less likely to get breast cancer diagnosis from routine screening | Breast cancer | The Guardian
description: Exclusive: People from marginalised groups more likely to be diagnosed via urgent referral or in emergency setting, research finds
Author: Tobi Thomas
Headline: Exclusive: People from marginalised groups more likely to be diagnosed via urgent referral or in emergency setting, research finds
Content: People from Black, Asian and mixed backgrounds 33% less likely to be diagnosed with breast cancer via routine screening.Photograph: By Ian Miles-Flashpoint Pictures/AlamyView image in fullscreenPeople from Black, Asian and mixed backgrounds 33% less likely to be diagnosed with breast cancer via routine screening.Photograph: By Ian Miles-Flashpoint Pictures/AlamyBreast cancerEthnic minorities in England less likely to get breast cancer diagnosis from routine screeningExclusive: People from marginalised groups more likely to be diagnosed via urgent referral or in emergency setting, research findsTobi ThomasHealth and inequalities correspondentSun 25 Oct 2026 09.28 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 11.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePeople from minority ethnic backgrounds in Englandare up to a third less likely to be diagnosed with breast cancer via routine screening, and are more likely to be diagnosed in an emergency setting, analysis has found.The research, carried out by academics at the University of Surrey and funded by the charity BreastCancerNow, involved analysis of 86,564 adults diagnosed with the disease between 2009 and 2019, from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink and the Cancer Registration Tumour and Treatment datasets.The analysis found that people from Black, Asian and mixed backgrounds, alongside people from deprived backgrounds, were up to 33% less likely to be diagnosed with breast cancer via screening, while these groups were also up to 31% more likely to be diagnosed via urgent suspected cancer referral, and up to 37% more likely to be diagnosed via emergency presentation.Manveet Basra, the associate director of public health, inclusion and awareness at Breast Cancer Now, said the analysis revealed that people from marginalised groups “face inequalities at every stage of their breast cancer experience, and tragically this impacts their survival rates”.Basra added: “This research helps us understand who is less likely to be diagnosed with breast cancer via screening, [who] might wait longer to get diagnosed or experience delays in treatment, and knowing what barriers they face enables us to work towards eliminating them.“Determined to improve breast cancer care and survival rates outcomes, we’re funding world-class research that actively identifies and addresses inequities, working with policymakers to improve equal access to screening, and ensuring our information, campaigns and life-changing support services reflect the diverse needs of everyone affected by this devastating disease.”Breast cancer is the most common cancer worldwide among women. It accounts for about one in four cases of cancer and is one of the leading causes of death in women under 50. Identifying women at higher risk early can pave the way for additional screening or preventive treatment.The research also revealed that people living with a learning disability faced poorer cancer outcomes: their time to diagnosis was 18% longer than people without a learning disability, and they faced a 10% longer wait time for treatment.NHS urges breast cancer patients from minority backgrounds to participate in trialsRead moreThis research adds to existing evidence of the unequal outcomes people from marginalised backgrounds face in regards to cancer.A previous study showed thatethnic minorities required more visits to GPs than other people before being diagnosed with cancer. On average, one in five people across England require three or more GP interactions before being diagnosed with cancer. But for people from ethnic minority backgrounds, the figure rises to one in three, according to analysis of the NHS cancer patient experience 2022 survey by QualityWatch, a joint programme from the Nuffield Trust and the Health Foundation.Research from the UK Health Security Agency has also suggested thatyoung black women are more likely to have aggressive breast cancer tumours, experience poorer care and have higher mortality rates, but are significantly under-represented in clinical research.Dr Rob Kerrison, an associate professor of cancer care and co-lead of the cancer care expert group at the University of Surrey and the lead investigator of this study, said: “We know that some groups of women in the UK have poorer breast cancer survival than others, but until now we have had only a limited understanding of why. Our findings suggest that inequalities in access to screening and timely treatment may be part of the explanation.“Women from a range of disadvantaged and under-served groups were less likely to have their cancer detected through screening and often waited longer to start treatment. If we are serious about improving breast cancer outcomes, we need to ensure that everyone can access screening and receive prompt treatment, regardless of their background or circumstances.”Explore more on these topicsBreast cancerInequalityHealthRacePovertyNHSEnglandnewsShareReuse this content

title: Anthropic sued for allegedly using 274 Elvis Presley songs to train AI models | US news | The Guardian
description: Authentic Brands Group says AI company infringed on rights of songs by the King such as Can’t Help Falling in Love
Author: Marina Dunbar
Headline: Authentic Brands Group says AI company infringed on rights of songs by the King such as Can’t Help Falling in Love
Content: ‘The defendant … has built its entire business model based on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before,’ the lawsuit says.Photograph: Universal Pictures. All Rights Reserved./PAView image in fullscreen‘The defendant … has built its entire business model based on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before,’ the lawsuit says.Photograph: Universal Pictures. All Rights Reserved./PAUS newsAnthropic sued for allegedly using 274 Elvis Presley songs to train AI modelsAuthentic Brands Group says AI company infringed on rights of songs by the King such as Can’t Help Falling in LoveMarina DunbarSun 25 Oct 2026 14.25 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 14.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe owners ofElvis Presley’s music catalogue are suing artificial intelligence (AI) companyAnthropicfor allegedly using Presley’s songs to train their models without permission.Authentic Brands Group, the licensing organization that has ownership of both Presley’s music and likeness, is accusing Anthropic of infringing on the rights of 274 songs by Presley. The lawsuit, first reported byBillboard, was filed on Friday.While AI firms have already facedcopyright infringement claimsfrom the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) andmusic labelssuch as Sony,Universaland Warner Records, this case represents one of the first major legal challenges brought directly by an artist’s estate against an AI developer. The result could set a broader precedent for how AI companies are allowed to use existing music catalogues.“The Elvis plaintiffs bring this action to enforce these exclusive rights against the defendant that has built its entire business model based on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before,” lead attorney Richard Busch wrote in the lawsuit.The lawsuit claims that “from its inception, Anthropic’s AI model, ‘Claude,’ has created infringing output of copyrighted material of virtually every song from every catalog available on the internet”.It further accuses Anthropic of utilizing 274 of Presley’s songs to train its AI model. These works include Can’t Help Falling in Love, All Shook Up and A Little Less Conversation. The plaintiffs are seeking $150,000 per infringed track, or about $41m (about £31m).skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every daySign up toHeadlines USGet the most important US headlines and highlights emailed direct to you every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAnthropic sued over alleged theft of ‘tens of thousands’ of songsRead more“Even Anthropic’s institution of guardrails (albeit ineffectively) to purportedly limit outputs which infringe upon music copyrights, after being caught, along with its knowledge that its guardrails were ineffective to stop creating outputs which infringed music copyrights, demonstrates that Anthropic knowingly engaged and continues to willfully engage in copyright infringement of others’ musical works,” the lawsuit states.AI music platforms work by analyzing large amounts of recorded music in order to learn the sounds, structures and expressions of songs, and then allows users to create their own AI-generated music via text or speech prompts.Musicians haverepeatedlyexpressed concernsthat their music and voices are being used without their permission by AI models, as well asfears thatAI-generated “slop” musiccould replacehuman-made songs.Some AI bots have even begunimpersonatingreal living artists on music streaming platforms. title: ‘They paved paradise’: fighting back over the loss of green spaces in Cameroon’s capital | Global development | The Guardian
description: Concrete sprawl in Yaoundé has devastated the city’s trees and parks, so volunteers are stepping up, shrub by shrub
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Concrete sprawl in Yaoundé has devastated the city’s trees and parks, so volunteers are stepping up, shrub by shrub
Content: Jean-Baptiste Tchengang, a self-taught gardener, in his plot in Nkolbisson, on the outskirts of Yaoundé. The city’s green space has fallen from 28.6% to just 5.4%.Photograph: Christian EssimiView image in fullscreenJean-Baptiste Tchengang, a self-taught gardener, in his plot in Nkolbisson, on the outskirts of Yaoundé. The city’s green space has fallen from 28.6% to just 5.4%.Photograph: Christian EssimiGlobal development‘They paved paradise’: fighting back over the loss of green spaces in Cameroon’s capitalConcrete sprawl in Yaoundé has devastated the city’s trees and parks, so volunteers are stepping up, shrub by shrubSupported byAbout this contentChristian Essimi in YaoundéSun 25 Oct 2026 11.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 14.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAlittle piece of paradise is buried under the asphalt that is now lined with parked cars. The romantic spot where Sosthène Hugues Ngono used to bring his first dates had been green and beautiful. “It wasn’t just a park,” he says, standing at the edge of what is now a private car park in Cameroon’s capital, Yaoundé.“It was where I came to clear my head when things felt confused,” he says. “Where I met people; where I fell in love, more than once.”Ngono, 36, a mathematics teacher, watched in dismay as the public park in Essos, a densely populated neighbourhood of Yaoundé, was razed in February last year, but his loss was only a small, personal version of a larger one playing out across the city.Green space in Yaoundé is under mounting pressure from unregulated urban expansion. Yaoundé covered nearly 33 sq miles (85 sq km) in 1984. By 2024 it had spread to cover 181 sq miles, according to astudy by the University of Yaoundé.Over the same period, the share of wooded areas in the city’s land cover dropped from 28.6% to just 5.4%.Yaoundé’s rapid development reflects growing demand for housing and infrastructure as its population expands. TheUN put the capital’s population at 5.1 millionin 2025. Cameroon’s housing ministry estimated a nationalhousing deficit of 2.5m unitsin 2020, most acutely felt in the city.With formal housing supply falling far short of demand, much of Yaoundé’s growth has taken the form of informal settlements and slums, often built without permits over the valleys, wetlands and hillsides of its green belt.However, its disappearance has given rise to a quiet counter-movement. Jean-Baptiste Tchengang, a 34-year-old self-taught gardener, grows mostly ornamental plants, decorative foliage and small shrubs suited to Yaoundé’s climate, chosen because they multiply easily and fit into small yards.“Their value is as much practical as it is beautiful,” he says. “They bring colour and coolness, but they also give people a simple way to rebuild small green spaces where the big gardens are disappearing.”Since 2022, Tchengang has run community workshops on composting and preserving local plant species from his own plot in Nkolbisson, a district on Yaoundé’s outskirts that researchers identify as one of the city’s historic areas of urban expansion, dating from 1984.“I have trained or helped about 300 people since I started,” he says. Ten of his trainees have gone on to build their own gardens on abandoned plots, providing vegetables, medicinal plants and social spaces.View image in fullscreenJean-Baptiste Tchengang in his garden in Nkolbisson.Photograph: Christian Essimi“Getting access to land is the hardest part,” Tchengang says. “There’s no funding, plants get stolen, and the ones you can buy are scarce and expensive. But somehow, I make it work.”When funds allow, Yaoundé city council buys shrubs and gets him to plant and maintain them, but it is not regular work. In July, Tchengang brought together about 50 young nature conservation volunteers who wanted to learn his methods to make their own case to the authorities. Trees especially have been suffering, disappearing from the urban landscape.“Trees are not there simply to make Yaoundé more beautiful,” says Jean-Marie Essoh, a climate specialist in the city. “They absorb rainwater, slow runoff and help hold the soil together.“They also cool a city where concrete keeps spreading,” he says. “When they disappear, it weakens far more than the landscape.”As trees are carbon sinks, absorbing CO2, their disappearance makes climate adaptation harder in a city regularly hit by heavy rains and flooding; when they are felled, that carbon is released back into the atmosphere.A 2023report on urban forestsby the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) found that trees and green spaces play a vital role in climate resilience and warned that their benefits are increasingly under threat as cities expand.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every fortnightSign up toGlobal DispatchGet a different world view with a roundup of the best news, features, opinion and photography, curated by our global development teamEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionKnowing where those benefits are being lost is the starting point for Mireille Nonga’s work. A 33-year-old urban-planning student at the University of Yaoundé I, she has mapped the city’s green spaces with 20 classmates since 2023, identifying 10 potential sites for reforestation.“There are several criteria,” says Nonga. “First, the position of the plot in relation to urban development in the area, its availability and its land status, whether it belongs to the state.Other points to consider, she says, are “accessibility, access to water and the flow of people around it”.From the ashes: how a mayor beat the loggers to turn the Amazon green againRead moreToday, the Sainte-Anastasie wood and the nearby garden at Place Charles Atangana are among the few green spaces remaining in Yaoundé. According to Nonga, even these central spaces are inconsistently maintained.Yaoundé’s authorities do recognise the problem.
