collecting what is due from smaller merchants selling on their platforms.On top of that, there have been stories indicating the level of headroom the chancellor will be looking at – in the region of £15bn – known in the political trade as “pitch rolling” to avoid alarming the markets or the public.The Treasury and No 10 have also undertaken their traditional stream of embargoed announcements by press release in the days before the fiscal event, such as a new£1.5bn borrowing facility for local authoritiesand £1bn for social housing, as they seek to build a sense of action and momentum about what the government is trying to achieve.Former Treasury advisers believe the rigamarole around budget security is partly designed to deter civil servants and gossiping MPs from thinking they can embark on unauthorised chatter before a policy is ready.View image in fullscreenFormer Treasury advisers think the rigamarole is partly designed to deter Westminster gossips.Photograph: David Levene/The GuardianBut they also say it is unhelpful for the chancellor to produce a hermetically sealed budget, which could cause a backlash over surprise measures – in the markets, the media, among the government’s own MPs and the wider public.It is often the less-trailed policies that have tended to go wrong, from George Osborne’s pasty tax in 2012 to Philip Hammond’s surprise national insurance hike for the self-employed in 2017 that had to be abandoned within seven days after a furore among Conservative MPs about breaking their manifesto promise.Aides say there is a balance to be struck – and it’s not always a good idea to hoard information until budget day. “If everything is kept tight, then you end up surprising people. And that’s called a Liz Truss situation,” says one former strategist from the Tory years.View image in fullscreenLiz Truss resigned as prime minister in 2022 after her government’s mini-budget crashed the markets.Photograph: Alberto Pezzali/APHealey has been shutting down speculation about various tax rises, from higher capital gains tax on certain assets to lowering the mansion tax on properties worth more than £1.5m – showing he has begun to see the virtue in expectation management and limiting surprises on the big day.There may still be a few fiscal “rabbits out of the hat” on the day, as Healey seeks to combine a “steady-as-she-goes” budget with some eye-catching measures designed to show the public that the government is on their side.But if the Treasury really has aimed for military levels of secrecy around its budget, theMinistry of Defencemight have something to worry about.Explore more on these topicsBudget 2026John HealeyTax and spendingBanks and building societiesEnergy billsDefence policyMinistry of DefenceanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan | US news | The Guardian
description: Trump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’
Author: Victoria Bekiempis
Headline: Trump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’
Content: Nicki Minaj and Donald Trump attend a rally on Sunday in Port Huron, Michigan, for Republican Mike Rogers before the midterm elections.Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/ReutersView image in fullscreenNicki Minaj and Donald Trump attend a rally on Sunday in Port Huron, Michigan, for Republican Mike Rogers before the midterm elections.Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/ReutersUS newsTrump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in MichiganTrump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’Victoria BekiempisSun 25 Oct 2026 18.36 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDonald Trumpreiterated his apparent love for buxom bums during a rally inMichiganon Sunday where he encouraged the crowd to compliment rapperNicki Minaj’s behind.Trump’s cheeky comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recentobservationon the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end. Earlier in October, Trumpsaidof the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass and I looked at the whole – and then I looked at his hands. Look at his hands. He’s got these, like, claws.“You are a great athlete,” Trumpalso saidto Husted. “Congratulations.”Trump was speaking at the rally to supportMike Rogers, the Michigan Republican Senate candidate. The Michigan race between Rogers and DemocratAbdul El-Sayedremains neck and neck as both political parties scramble for control of Congress in theupcomingmidterm elections. But he couldn’t resist his purported other favorite topic.View image in fullscreenMike Rogers gestures while with his wife, Kristi Clemens Rogers; Republican gubernatorial nominee John James; musician Nicki Minaj; and David Beamer, the father of Todd Beamer, during a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday.Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/ReutersThis afternoon, Trump said the media buzz about these comments was “fake news” neglecting the athletic context of his statements. Trump said he had just learned Husted was a college athlete when he was “looking at him up and down, and I’m studying him”.Michigan residents fight potential $6.4bn datacenter bill: ‘That is insanity’Read moreTrump insisted his subsequent crack was “in fun”. “I said: I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. It’s true. Off the record, women yes, men no, OK.”Trump then shouted out Minaj, who the New York Post said wasdonnedin “head-to-toe Gucci” today. Minaj, the paper also reported, was seen walking with Trump after leaving Air Force One.“By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before –Nicki Minaj,” Trump said, prompting celebratory woos from the crowd. “That’s hard to miss. That – stand up! That’s hard to miss.“OK, I’m going to get back to my story, Nicki,” Trump continued following still more cheers. “I hope Nicki wasn’t insulted, but we love Nicki. She’sbeen with usfor a long time.”Trump made statements about Husted’s tush just over a week ago in Kentucky.“I examined his ass,” Trump said of Husted, who was not at the event. “And then I looked at his shoulders. I looked at his feet. I looked at his hand. I looked at his jawline. Studied him. He’s got a jawline.View image in fullscreenBrian Pannebecker, the Auto Workers for Trump founder, stands with Donald Trump during a Mike Rogers rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday.Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/Reuters“I then patted him on the shoulder, and it was like a piece of steel. I’m still recovering,” Trump said.Trump also recently praised the appearance of Ed Gallrein, theRepublican congressional candidate from Kentucky.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly, plus breaking news alertsSign up toThe Stakes 2026A weekly guide to what really matters in the US midterms, plus breaking news alerts.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionObama rallies rapturous Michigan crowd for El-Sayed: ‘He’ll finish the job we started’Read more“I needed somebody good, and this guy walks through the door,” Trump remarked of Gallrein, in describing his efforts to find a replacement for anti-Maga incumbent Thomas Massie. “I said, look at this beautiful guy.”The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about why Trump has been discussing others’ bodies.Trump’s comments come amid criticism of his language style, which some have likened to grotesquerie.During a Saturday rally for El-Sayed, Barack Obamajokedabout Trump’s White Houserenovationefforts.“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the former president said.Meanwhile, Trump said that the US-Canada trade war wouldsoonbe in America’s rear view.“Canada has been ripping off the US for years. I had to do it,” Trump said of tariffs during the rally. “We’ll have that settled pretty soon. They’re willing to give us anything at this moment.”Explore more on these topicsUS newsUS politicsMichiganDonald TrumpNicki MinajRepublicansUS CongressnewsShareReuse this content

title: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash | Alaska | The Guardian
description: Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries after a driver struck the car transporting group to campaign stop
Author: Coral Murphy Marcos
Headline: Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries after a driver struck the car transporting group to campaign stop
Content: Mary Peltola participates in a debate in Anchorage, Alaska, on 15 October.Photograph: Kerry Tasker/ReutersView image in fullscreenMary Peltola participates in a debate in Anchorage, Alaska, on 15 October.Photograph: Kerry Tasker/ReutersAlaskaAlaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crashPeltola and her family sustained minor injuries after a driver struck the car transporting group to campaign stopCoral Murphy Marcosand agenciesSun 25 Oct 2026 16.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMary Peltola, a Democrat who is running forAlaska’s lone US Senate seat, and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash while driving to a campaign stop on Saturday, her campaign said.The family was on its way to theAlaskaFederation of Natives annual banquet when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, her campaign said in a statement on Sunday. Peltola required medical attention after the collision.“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” Cheryl Bruce, Peltola’s campaign manager, said in astatement. “Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover.”Bruce added: “Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families.”Police responded to a “multi-vehicle collision” at about 6.55pm on Saturday, according to the Anchorage police department. Peltola’s family and the occupant of a second vehicle were taken to a local hospital “with non-life-threatening injuries”, according to the authorities, while the occupant of a third vehicle refused medical transport.View image in fullscreenMary Peltola, center, celebrates with her family and supporters as ranked-choice tabulations were announced in November 2022 in Anchorage, Alaska.Photograph: Loren Holmes/AP“The circumstances of the collision are under investigation,” reads astatementfrom the police department.Peltola, an Alaska Native and former congresswoman, is challenging Republican incumbent senatorDan Sullivan, hoping to become the first Democrat in nearly two decades to represent the state in the Senate. Both candidates have tried to rally support from Alaska Native voters, a key constituency in thehigh-stakes racethat has become one of the most watched in the nation.On Friday, Donald Trumporderedthe justice department to block the certification of the Senate election in Alaska if Sullivan loses. The lawsuit cites potential confusion with another Republican candidate who is listed on the ranked-choice ballot asDaniel J Sullivan Jr, who is a retired schoolteacher.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly, plus breaking news alertsSign up toThe Stakes 2026A weekly guide to what really matters in the US midterms, plus breaking news alerts.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPeltola’s incident delayed what her campaign announced as the “Alaska Always tour,” an eight-stop push through the last week before election day. Her campaign said she will resume events on Tuesday, with a stop in Homer, Alaska.Explore more on these topicsAlaskaUS SenateUS midterm elections 2026US CongressUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Suspect in shooting death of Missouri teen on highway charged in second road incident | Missouri | The Guardian
description: Man accused of shooting teen who was driving to a party is also linked to shooting of a vehicle days earlier, police say
Author: Jessica Glenza
Headline: Man accused of shooting teen who was driving to a party is also linked to shooting of a vehicle days earlier, police say
Content: Alyssa Wilson, 17, was shot and killed as she drove down Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri, on 14 October.Photograph: Courtesy Robert HickmanView image in fullscreenAlyssa Wilson, 17, was shot and killed as she drove down Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri, on 14 October.Photograph: Courtesy Robert HickmanMissouriSuspect in shooting death of Missouri teen on highway charged in second road incidentMan accused of shooting teen who was driving to a party is also linked to shooting of a vehicle days earlier, police sayJessica GlenzaSun 25 Oct 2026 15.12 EDTFirst published on Sun 25 Oct 2026 10.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA man accused in the shooting death of aMissouriteen has been charged in a second shooting incident – both of which involve firing into cars on the highway.Alyssa Wilson, 17, was shot and killed as she drove down Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri, on 14 October. The teen was on her way to a Halloween party at St Louis Zoo, called Boo at the Zoo, when a suspect fired a single shot into the back of Wilson’s Buick Encore.The shot struck Wilson in the back, incapacitated her, and sent her crashing into a concrete highway median, according to prosecutors. She was pronounced dead at Barnes-Jewish Hospital.The suspected shooter, Willie James Herndon, 43, of Texas, had no known relationship to the teen.“Alyssa was 17, excited about her life, excited about her future,” her father Robert Hickman said, asstate charges were announced. “She had 60 days until she turned 18, and we were getting ready to take our first family vacation together to go to Disney for her to see her favorite person in the world, Princess Tiana, and unfortunately, she’s not going to get to do that any more. This was a senseless act.”Now, federal court documents show that Herndon has been charged in a second shooting incident, this one just a few days earlier.On 11 October, St Louis metropolitan police received a report that a vehicle was shot just after exiting Interstate 55 in Missouri. Surveillance footage captured a white SUV fleeing the scene – a vehicle that matched the appearance of Herndon’s Buick Enclave.A shell casing was also recovered from the scene. Prosecutors said they were conducting ballistics tests to determine if it was fired from the same weapon that killed Wilson.In a federal criminal complaint, prosecutors lay out how they tracked what appeared to be Herndon’s Buick Enclave from the first shooting incident on 11 October, then the scene of Wilson’s death on 14 October, to a Days Inn in Caseyville, Illinois 16 October.There, prosecutors approached Herndon’s wife Taiya Herndon, 45, and were speaking to her when Herndon “emerged” from the hotel room and began to flee. As he was arrested, he was “screaming words about a shooting”, prosecutors said.Inside the Days Inn hotel room, prosecutors said they found a ABC-15 rifle “in plain view”, ammunition that matched the kind used in Wilson’s shooting, a receipt from a gas station near the scene of Wilson’s death on Interstate 170, two license plates and handwritten notes describing police vehicles Herndon believed were tracking him.Federal prosecutors in Illinois have charged Herndon with being a felon in possession of a firearm. He has separately been charged with first-degree murder and armed criminal action in St Louis county, Missouri. His federal public defender did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Explore more on these topicsMissouriGun crimeUS crimenewsShareReuse this content

title: US south-west braces for more storms after enduring days of rain and flooding | US weather | The Guardian
description: More inclement weather forecast in rain-soaked Four Corners region after evacuations and rescues last week
Author: Coral Murphy Marcos
Headline: More inclement weather forecast in rain-soaked Four Corners region after evacuations and rescues last week
Content: People traverse a cordoned-off street as floodwaters from the San Juan River rise in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, on Friday.Photograph: Emilija Jefremova/ReutersView image in fullscreenPeople traverse a cordoned-off street as floodwaters from the San Juan River rise in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, on Friday.Photograph: Emilija Jefremova/ReutersUS weatherUS south-west braces for more storms after enduring days of rain and floodingMore inclement weather forecast in rain-soaked Four Corners region after evacuations and rescues last weekCoral Murphy Marcosand agenciesSun 25 Oct 2026 15.02 EDTFirst published on Sun 25 Oct 2026 13.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAnother round of heavy showers and thunderstorms were expected to hit the south-west US on Sunday after the region endured days of rain that forced evacuations, water rescues and multi-million-dollar damage.The National Weather Serviceissueda flood watch for much of the Four Corners – the meeting point of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah – even as local officials forecast further receding of swollen rivers that surged since rains picked up on Wednesday.About 4ft (1 meter) of water flooded the home of Shane Ferrari, the sheriff of San Juan county,New Mexico. He said the area’s situation was stable on Sunday, but he and other residents were trying to clean up and deal with damage.The New Mexico governor, Michelle Lujan Grisham, said in a statement on Saturday that law enforcement had reported hundreds of water rescues between the cities of Farmington and Bloomfield.View image in fullscreenFlooding in the Gould Wash drainage watercourse in Hurricane, Utah, on Thursday.Photograph: Landon Christensen/AP“Families in Bloomfield and Farmington spent the night on rooftops watching the river flood their homes, and our national guard and state police crews have been bringing them to safety,” said Lujan Grisham. “Right now, our focus is saving lives. If you’re told to evacuate, go. Once the water recedes, the state will do everything in its power to help San Juan county families rebuild.”“No deaths have been reported,” she added.The San Juan River in Farmington on Friday ran 2 ft above its previousrecordset in 1909.San Juan county spokesperson Devin Neeley said the county did not have official numbers on damage to homes or the number of people evacuated, but he was not aware of any loss of life.View image in fullscreenPickup trucks are submerged along Highway 160 in South Fork, Colorado, on Friday.Photograph: South Fork Fire Rescue/APNeeley said the flood waters were receding but left mud and silt, much of which has been contaminated with sewage because of failures at waste plants. There were still power outages affecting multiple areas, and it would probably be a few days until residents got their power back on.“It’s a pretty active disaster zone,” he said. “We’re not on the downswing by any means.”The flooding is just the latest from two months of on-and-off heavy rain caused by tropical moisture coming ashore from the Pacific. After months of drought, other recent deadly flooding struck theGrand Canyonand areas of New Mexico.New Mexico has been hit with back-to-back weather events this weekend. A tornado struck Santa Fe on Saturday, damaging at least eight houses, including to roof collapses, according to astatementby the city of Santa Fe. No injuries were reported.Explore more on these topicsUS weatherFloodingNew MexicoColoradoArizonaUtahExtreme weathernewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron Cohen | Movies | The Guardian
description:
Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’

• This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?
Author: Catherine Shoard
Headline: Exclusive: Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’• This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?
Content: ‘I was a little offended. You’re picking on these Americans that aren’t the brightest’ … Loudermilk in the trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I?Photograph: Ali G: Who Iz I?View image in fullscreen‘I was a little offended. You’re picking on these Americans that aren’t the brightest’ … Loudermilk in the trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I?Photograph: Ali G: Who Iz I?Movies‘He’s not going to punk me. I’ll trick him’: Ali G: Who Iz I? stooge says he was in on joke but didn’t tell Sacha Baron CohenExclusive:Joshua Loudermilk says suspicions first raised during filming by gun shaped like wearable plastic bottom: ‘You’re gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that’This article contains spoilers for Ali G: Who Iz I?Catherine ShoardSun 25 Oct 2026 12.13 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 12.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJoshua Loudermilk, one of two men apparently discredited by the new Ali G movieAli G: Who Iz I?, has said that he was in on the joke, but that the film-makers didn’t realise this.Loudermilk, a 54-year-old aspiring actor from North Carolina, has told the Guardian he recognised starSacha Baron Cohenearly in the shoot but continued pretending to be a hard-right Maga sympathiser prepared to defend the US border at all costs.The movie involves Loudermilk being recruited by another Cohen character, the ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad, to help form a citizens’ warrior force to protect US borders, making use of his top-secret new weapon: a gun disguised as buttocks.Along with fellow recruit Michael Aboud, the chair of the El Paso county Republican party, Loudermilk joins Morad on a mission to stop the birth on US soil of the baby of a fictional South American drugs kinpin. This involves abducting a woman apparently in labour, abandoning her in a deserted medical facility, kidnapping her newborn child (a lifelike prosthetic) and driving it in a zipped bag to the border in order to deliver it by drone to Mexico.Republican leader embarrassed by Ali G film says he plans to sue Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘A liar and a pervert’Read moreAboud is shown taking the decision to drop the child from a great height into Mexico rather than have it touch US soil. He has since called Cohen a “liar” and a “pervert” and expressed his intention to sue. The film repeatedly stresses that both men were “not in on it”.Loudermilk has told the Guardian he was surprised the production company did not notice social media updates he posted shortly after the shoot in which he named Cohen and expressed his excitement about the project.But rather than being upset about his involvement, Loudermilk – who recently appeared as Squire Dap in the North Carolina Town of Hudson Fall Dinner Theatre’s production of Camelot – says he welcomes the publicity boost.“I want to use this to my benefit,” he says. “I would hope Sacha would read this and laugh, like: ‘Hey, you got me!’ I had so much fun creating that character. I was trying to see if I was any good at acting in comedy. And I realised: ‘Oh, I think I’m good at this.’ And that’s what I wanna do for the rest of my life.”View image in fullscreenJoshua Loudermilk.Photograph: Joshua LoudermilkHis experience began in September 2025 when Loudermilk spotted apost on Craigslistby a body called the American Citizen Initiative (whose website is no longer active) recruiting “patriotic legal Americans” “concerned about the border crisis” who “believe that illegal immigration is out of control”.The ad, one of dozens posted across US states simultaneously, invited “real American citizens” to “attend an exclusive, hands-on event experience where you’ll learn the truth about what’s happening on the border and how you can make a difference”. Attendees were promised $300 as well as travel expenses.“I was like: this seems kind of weird,” says Loudermilk, who describes himself as broadly apolitical. “I don’t really care much about our borders. My mom’s from Ireland.”Recently made redundant, his motivation for responding was primarily financial. “I know rightwing and leftwing organisations have money and will pay people to just hold a sign up. I remember thinking: I wanna get on that gravy train. I want some George Soros money. I’ll pretend to be whatever. Just let me feed my family. It could have been save the whales and I would have done it.”In his application, Loudermilk fabricated hard-right views, mentioned that he had been a preacher and neglected to declare his ambitions to become a comedy actor – in part, he says, out of embarrassment. He then filled in a “silly questionnaire – very obvious, very slanted to the right”.Loudermilk was then called for a video interview, which involved the identification of left-leaning celebrities, as well as figures including Borat, Cohen’s bumbling Kazakh reporter, who Loudermilk duly named.He was also asked if he was a Trump supporter. “The funny thing is: not really. He’s just a leader. But I was like: I’m going to be an improv actor so I said: ‘Yeah, I support Trump!’ Next thing I know they’re like, ‘We want you to come out to be a part of this.’The company flew him to Ontario, California, with an initial offer of $1,000, plus food and expenses, on top of which Loudermilk received a further $700. “It was all real secretive. They frisked me down and I got in a truck to go to a karate studio.”Once he arrived, Loudermilk was greeted by security and informed an Israeli commander wanted to meet him. “That was a red flag. Why would Israeli commander be in America? I go in there and immediately I see this really tall guy with this horrible plastic surgery. My first thought was: that looks like Sacha Cohen. But I was like: nah, that can’t be him.”View image in fullscreenSacha Baron Cohen as ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad in the 2018 show Who is America?Photograph: ShowtimeLoudermilk’s suspicions were further raised, he says, when he met his fellow recruits. “They were old, old, old white guys who were really out of shape. Everyone’s wearing these Trump shirts. They didn’t seem like warriors. I thought: they could probably get better people for this.”Morad then produced the top-secret new gun in the shape of large, strap-on bottom, out of which bullets are fired from the anus. Initially, Loudermilk was baffled by its logistics. “I kept thinking: no-one’s gonna wear that thing because your butt’s gonna be abnormally large. No one has a butt like that. Are you gonna put a butt on top of a butt? You can’t run in that. And you’d have to wear some really big khaki pants.”He volunteered to be first to try the weapon out, whereupon Morad demonstrated the trigger system, which involves the pumping of an attached rubber penis. “And he kept calling it ‘shmeckel’. I’m like: that’s Sacha Cohen. At that moment I knew it.“And I was like: oh no, I can’t break character. I’ve got to go along with it. So what I decided [was] that whatever he did, I was going to take it another step further. He’s not going to punk me; I’m going to trick him. So I decided to get into character and just have a good time because they’re paying me.”As the plot became more “ridiculous”, says Loudermilk, so his enjoyment increased. During a scene in which he, Morad and Aboud help deliver the (prosthetic) baby, the three men become covered with fake excrement. “This big blast of pooping pap,” recalls Loudermilk – but he was reassured after inadvertently sampling some of the fluids. “I thought: ‘This doesn’t taste bad.’ So I just kind of hung in there. It was disgusting, but I was having fun.”View image in fullscreenLoudermilk and Aboud in Ali G: Who Iz I?Photograph: Ali G: Who Iz I?At the climax at the Mexican border, says Loudermilk, he handed the remote control to the drone to Aboud, “because that was boring. It was ridiculous – they’re not flying a real baby”. Instead, he “wanted to have fun with Sacha,” so he grabbed the “butt-gun”, yelling about the need to defend themselves, and eventually discharged fire, aided by Morad, who helps pump the penis trigger.Loudermilk declines to defend Aboud’s decision to then endanger the life of the baby by dropping it from the drone, but expresses some sympathy for his unwitting co-star.“I felt sorry for the poor fella. Because I’m all-in and he’s just kind of following me around like in a daze, like: what’s happening? He was scared to death, and obviously very uncomfortable, bless his heart.“I’d never met the guy before, but [at times] it felt he was totally freaking out on me. So I had to make him believe that I believed all this. So I would tell him, ‘You’re being a wimp, man. Our freedom is on the line.’ I kept trying to keep him from quitting.“But I’m surprised he didn’t figure it out. Like, come on, Michael – why would they recruit you to defend our border? Think about it.”Loudermilk concedes his decision to maintain the pretence of being far-right once he had worked out the true nature of the project was in part because he “was a little offended. Like: really? You’re picking on these Americans that aren’t the brightest. You’re gonna make fun of them and they’re not gonna know any better. So I decided I needed to be their ally, even though I’m not that way.”View image in fullscreenBaron Cohen at the film’s Los Angeles premiere.Photograph: Mario Anzuoni/ReutersAt the end of filming, Loudermilk signed a non-disclosure agreement at the request of the production company, which he says he was not given a copy of, and which mostly related to the top-secret weapons. “They came up to me after I was done and said, ‘Oh, you did so well!’ I said, ‘You get what you need? Can I talk about it?’ They said, ‘Oh no, not yet. Especially the butt-gun.’”Loudermilk considers any such terms breached now the film is out and mentions him by name: “It’s fair game.” He adds that, after shooting, he had some qualms about not coming clean to them that he had twigged. “I felt a little bad. And that’s why I thought: I should make a little post.”In December last year, Loudermilk posted three times on his public Facebook page about “eight hours of intense filming one on one with Sasha [sic] Cohen”, as well as twice on his Instagram, which is also public.“But they never saw it. And the fact they missed that makes it even better to me. So I guess it’s on them.”Last week, representatives for the film confirmed again to the Guardian that Loudermilk was not in on the joke. They have not yet responded to a further followup question on this.The film was released nationwide in the UK on Friday, as well as in a limited run in the US. Loudermilk, who has not yet watched it, says he is unconcerned about the prospect of recriminations from anyone upset by his apparent actions.“That people would be disgusted is a compliment. Oh, I really did a good job, huh! I pulled it off and I was so proud of myself.”Explore more on these topicsFilmAli G: Who Iz IRepublicansSacha Baron CohenFilm industryComedy filmsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Volkswagen to build $4bn Audi SUV factory in US despite job cuts at home | Volkswagen (VW) | The Guardian
description: VW investment, creating 4,500 jobs in Georgia, comes amid Trump’s damaging tariffs, intense Chinese competition and costly shift towards EVs
Author: Jasper Jolly
Headline: VW investment, creating 4,500 jobs in Georgia, comes amid Trump’s damaging tariffs, intense Chinese competition and costly shift towards EVs
Content: Audi’s chief executive, Gernot Döllner, joined Trump on stage at a rally on Saturday to announce the factory in Macon, Georgia.Photograph: Friso Gentsch/EPAView image in fullscreenAudi’s chief executive, Gernot Döllner, joined Trump on stage at a rally on Saturday to announce the factory in Macon, Georgia.Photograph: Friso Gentsch/EPAVolkswagen (VW)Volkswagen to build $4bn Audi SUV factory in US despite job cuts at homeVW investment, creating 4,500 jobs in Georgia, comes amid Trump’s damaging tariffs, intense Chinese competition and costly shift towards EVsJasper Jollyand agenciesSun 25 Oct 2026 09.43 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 11.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAudi has said it will spend $4bn (£3bn) to build its first factory in the US, as its parent company, Volkswagen, struggles with the impact of steep tariffs imposed by Donald Trump.The German brand’s chief executive, Gernot Döllner, joined Trump on stage at a campaign rally on Saturday night to announce the factory in Macon,Georgia, in an unusual move by a big European brand just days before the US midterm elections.The Republican party under Trump is trying to retain control of both houses of Congress, butit is polling poorlyas it struggles withhigher fuel prices caused by Trump’s war on Iran, as well as his trade war against some of the US’s biggest trading partners.Volkswagen to cut further 50,000 jobs as it ends row with union over revival planRead moreTrump has long tried to convince voters that his tariffs are helping to increase the number of manufacturing jobs in the US, and has seized on any new factory investments. However, US vehicle and parts employment has fallen since Trump took office last year.Audi, Volkswagen’s most important premium brand, hassuffered from Trump’s 15% tariffs on importsfrom the EU as well as the president’s efforts to cut sales of battery electric vehicles in favour of petrol cars.It said it aims to build 200,000 SUVs at the new US factory, creating 4,500 jobs. The factory will build the Q7, Q8 and Q9 SUVs, shifting some production from Bratislava in Slovakia.Volkswagen has said Trump’s tariffs cost it up to €5bn(£4.2bn)a year, before the impact of lower sales. The German manufacturer this month said it was still struggling with “continued high pressure from import tariffs”. The carmaker was also forced to shift some production of its cheapest cars, such as the Jetta saloon and Taos SUV, from Mexico to the US.The new factory may add to tensions in Germany, where Volkswagen has started tocut as many as 100,000 jobs and close factories. It has blamed the job losses on intense competition from Chinese carmakers, as well as the tariffs and a need to invest heavily in the shift to EVs for markets other than the US.Döllner said he accepted the invitation to speak at Trump’s rally out of respect for the US.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We are planning to bring our ⁠biggest and most premium SUVs, and produce them here in Macon, Georgia,” he said at the event. “This is a long-term investment because we believe in the American market.”Volkswagen’s chief executive, Oliver Blume, told investors in July that “US tariffs create a significant burden and restrict international trade”.However, the group has said there is still demand in the US for Audi’s large petrol SUVs, and it is planning its largest-ever SUV, the Q9, with the American market in mind. Large petrol-powered SUVs have played abig role in global carbon emissions.Explore more on these topicsVolkswagen (VW)Automotive industryGermanyUS economyTrump administrationTrump tariffsEconomicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: NFL roundup: Falcons spoil Niners’ undefeated start; Steelers win in Paris | NFL | The Guardian
description: Tampa Bay routed the Panthers in Baker Mayfield’s return to Carolina, while the 49ers are unbeaten no more after a visit to Atlanta
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Tampa Bay routed the Panthers in Baker Mayfield’s return to Carolina, while the 49ers are unbeaten no more after a visit to Atlanta
Content: The 49ers lost to the Falcons on Sunday despite outgaining them on offense.Photograph: Mike Stewart/APView image in fullscreenThe 49ers lost to the Falcons on Sunday despite outgaining them on offense.Photograph: Mike Stewart/APNFLNFL roundup: Falcons spoil Niners’ undefeated start; Steelers win in ParisBucs rout Panthers in Baker Mayfield’s returnBrowns move to 5-2 with late win over TitansJets hand Dolphins their first win of the seasonAgenciesSun 25 Oct 2026 16.48 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 20.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAtlanta Falcons 29-20 San Francisco 49ersMichael Penix Jr threw three touchdown passes, Atlanta scored 13 points off four turnovers and the Falcons handed the San Francisco 49ers their first loss, 29-20. San Francisco were already thin at wide receiver before its offense faced additional limitations when running back Christian McCaffrey missed much of the first half with a thigh injury. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions, one of them by rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels. Daniels also recovered a fumble by George Kittle. Penix threw scoring passes to Nick Muse, Kyle Pitts and Drake London as the Falcons snapped a two-game skid.Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders unionize after years of fighting for fair payRead moreMinnesota Vikings 16-10 Indianapolis ColtsHarrison Smith capped another dominant performance by Minnesota’s defense with the game-sealing interception, and the Vikings overcame another sluggish start to stay unbeaten with a 16-10 victory over the spiraling Indianapolis Colts. Linebacker Blake Cashman led the onslaught of pressure on Daniel Jones all afternoon with 12 tackles, two sacks, four passes defensed and three quarterback hits as the Vikings improved to 6-0 despite minimal production from the offense. The Colts fell to 2-5. Jones went 13 for 122 for 108 yards and lost 44 yards on four sacks, and Spencer Shrader missed two field goals in the second half.Green Bay Packers 17–20 Detroit LionsJake Bates made a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the Detroit Lions (4-2) a 20-17 win over the Green Bay Packers (4-3). The Lions have won two straight for the first time this season, putting them in third place in the NFC North behind Minnesota and Chicago. The Packers had a three-game winning streak stopped and dropped to last place in the NFC North, lamenting a lot of penalties that went against them. Packers kicker Trey Smack also missed two field goals.Denver Broncos 30–16 Arizona CardinalsThe Denver Broncos (5-2) beat the Arizona Cardinals (2-5), using big plays to secure the win. Bo Nix ran for a 62-yard touchdown, and RJ Harvey turned a short screen pass into a 52-yard score. The Cardinals have now lost 10 straight home games. Denver’s defense was dominant with 12 quarterback hits and three sacks. Nix’s long touchdown run came late in the second quarter, giving the Broncos a 13-6 lead. The Cardinals cut the deficit to 20-13 in the third quarter, but the Broncos responded with a 76-yard touchdown drive to control the game.Los Angeles Rams 35–21 Las Vegas RaidersMatthew Stafford threw for three touchdowns and the visiting Los Angeles Rams built a 28-3 second quarter ⁠lead in their win over the slumping Las Vegas Raiders. Stafford completed 23 of 29 passes for 195 ⁠yards and an ⁠interception as ​Los Angeles (3-4) snapped a two-game losing streak. Blake Corum added 93 yards and a score on 17 rushes as the ⁠Rams finished with 386 total yards. Kirk Cousins hit 26 of 44 throws for 295 yards and two touchdowns, but it wasn’t enough ⁠as Las Vegas (3-4) dropped their fourth straight game. The Raiders managed just 48 yards ​on 17 carries and abandoned the ‌run for most ‌of the second half.Miami Dolphins 28-25 New York JetsMalik Willis lead the Miami Dolphins to their first win of the season with a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets. It was the first win for Jeff Hafley as coach of the Dolphins, who avoided an 0-6 start for the first time since 2019. They scored on their first two drives and controlled most of the game. The Jets are 2-5 and made a late push, but Willis sealed the victory with a first down on fourth-and-1. Willis threw two touchdown passes and ran for a score. Geno Smith threw three touchdown passes and an interception for the Jets.Pittsburgh Steelers 16-10 New Orleans SaintsAaron Rodgers threw one touchdown pass and Chris Boswell kicked three field goals in Pittsburgh’s 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in the NFL’s first regular-season game in France. Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and scrambled for a key first down late in fourth quarter as the Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game. Linebacker Payton Wilson had a red zone interception of Tyler Shough in the third quarter and the Saints (2-5) couldn’t recover. New Orleans rushed for just 18 yards.‘The Bird Reich’: Atlanta Falcons roasted over throwback logo with Nazi resemblanceRead moreNew York Giants 27-21 Houston TexansDevin Singletary’s 30-yard touchdown run in overtime lifted the New York Giants to a 27-21 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday. Cam Skattebo had a 16-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter and his 42-yard scamper to set up Singletary’s game-winning run. He had 17 carries for 124 yards after not having a carry last Sunday following a costly fumble two weeks ago. JJ McCarthy moved the ball effectively for the Giants (4-2-1) in his first start of the season after coach John Harbaugh benched Jameis Winston. He was 20 of 28 for 252 yards in the stadium in which he won the national title with Michigan in January 2024. The Texans (2-5) got the ball first in overtime, but New York’s defense forced a three-and-out with Kayvon Thibodeaux dropping a potential interception on second down.Cincinnati Bengals 35-13 Baltimore RavensJoe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half, and the Cincinnati Bengals rebounded from a desultory first two quarters to beat Baltimore 35-13, handing the Ravens a second straight divisional loss with Lamar Jackson sidelined. Baltimore dominated the first half but led only 13-0 after settling for a couple short field goals. Then the Ravens blew a double-digit second-half lead for the second straight week and 10th time since the start of the 2022 season. Baltimore has outscored opponents by 65 points in the first half this season, while being outscored by 70 in the second.Cleveland Browns 27-24 Tennessee TitansDeshaun Watson has led his fifth game-winning drive in the fourth quarter this season. He connected with Harold Fannin Jr on a 36-yard catch-and run that set up Andre Szmyt’s 32-yard field goal as time expired, and the Cleveland Browns beat the Tennessee Titans 27-24 on Sunday for their fifth win in six games. Watson ran for a touchdown and threw for 308 yards. Quinshon Judkins ran for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards in his best game yet. The Titans were trying to string together back-to-back wins for the first time in nearly four years.Tampa Bay Buccaneers 43-13 Carolina PanthersBucky Irving ran for 106 yards and two touchdowns, and Tampa Bay forced four turnovers as the Buccaneers hammered the Carolina Panthers 43-13 on Sunday in Baker Mayfield’s return. Mayfield had missed the previous three games with a dislocated right thumb. He attempted just 11 passes and threw for 64 yards while wearing a protective glove on his right hand. That was more than enough for him to improve to 7-1 against the Panthers, including 6-1 since joining the Bucs. Mayfield didn’t need to do much because Tampa Bay’s run game, defense and special teams dominated. The Bucs had 258 yards on the ground.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester United board hold crisis talks over Carrick’s future and Howe approach | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick’s job as manager is in the balance after Manchester United’s 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth, with Eddie Howe remaining the preferred candidate
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Michael Carrick’s job as manager is in the balance after Manchester United’s 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth, with Eddie Howe remaining the preferred candidate
Content: Michael Carrick said ‘it’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it’ after Manchester United’s defeat by Bournemouth.Photograph: Gary Oakley/EPAView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick said ‘it’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it’ after Manchester United’s defeat by Bournemouth.Photograph: Gary Oakley/EPAManchester UnitedManchester United board hold crisis talks over Carrick’s future and Howe approachJob in balance after 3-0 home defeat by BournemouthHowe is director of football Jason Wilcox’s top candidateJamie Jacksonat Old TraffordSun 25 Oct 2026 15.24 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 17.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester United’s hierarchy are in crisis talks over whether or not to sack Michael Carrick as head coach after heoversaw another torrid defeat, against Bournemouth at Old ­Trafford on Sunday, that left his job in the balance.Carrick was defiant after the 3-0 humbling, insisting he was not expecting to be removed from his post. “I totally understand the situation,” Carrick said of his job prospects. “I’m not expecting anything in ­particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal and I love this place.”Michael Carrick on the brink after Manchester United are humiliated by BournemouthRead moreBut the United executive are actively ­considering his dismissal, the ­Guardian understands, with the expectation at the club being that Carrick will be sacked.Eddie Howe remains the preferred candidate of Jason Wilcox, United’s director of football, should there be a change in the dugout, with the former Newcastle manager’s extensive Premier League experience placing him ahead of other potential ­targets.Howe would be less expensive to bring in than Unai Emery, another admired candidate, given that Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.Julian Nagelsmann, the former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by Christopher ­Vivell, United’s head of ­recruitment, but Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim ­Ratcliffe, who ­controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte is another who may be in the frame.Carrick, who left Bruno Fernandes out of his starting lineup – insisting before kick-off that he did so for football reasons and not because of thecaptain’s criticismof his ­tactics after the midweek ­Champions League defeat at Como – said: “I’ll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, ­whatever decision is made on anything really. So that’s kind of it. I’m not expecting anything either way.“It’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know. I will always do my best for the football club and I won’t change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see.”United endured a sixth defeat in 12 games in all competitions after Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and ­Evanilson scored for Marco Rose’s side. They have won only once in the league this season and sit in 16th. Their last win was on 10 September, against Sabah in the Champions League.The club cannot announce a sacking until they inform the New York Stock Exchange, which is closed at weekends. When Ruben Amorim was sacked in January, the decision was taken on the Sunday night after the coach’s explosive press conference following a draw at Leeds, but was not announced until the next day.Carrick made a point of ­applauding the home supporters at the end of the match, pumping his hand to his chest as he walked past a supportive Stretford End. As soon as he disappeared down the tunnel, boos met Fernandes, who was following the manager, alongside other United players.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“It wasn’t a farewell from me,” ­Carrick said. “I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way.“To have that connection with the supporters, it’s mixed emotions, it’ll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support. The situation is where we are and we haven’t had results or performances that have been good enough.”On his decision to omit Fernandes, who was an unused substitute, ­Carrick said: “There’s always times when you’re trying to make decisions that are to change the course of play and made a difference, but those are the decisions we made today.”Harry Maguire, United’s captain in Fernandes’ absence, insisted that the squad were “fully behind” ­Carrick. He said: “Coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season.As individuals, we’re not ­playing well enough. We have to look at ­ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team. That’s every player that I’m talking about. When things aren’t going your way you have to do the basics well.”Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickEddie HoweBournemouthnewsShareReuse this content

title: Kimi Antonelli storms to US F1 GP victory but is made to wait for title glory | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: The 20-year-old championship leader won from Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen and should become F1’s youngest world champion next week in Mexico
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: The 20-year-old championship leader won from Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen and should become F1’s youngest world champion next week in Mexico
Content: Kimi Antonelli celebrates with the trophy on the podium after winning the US GP.Photograph: Mike Segar/ReutersView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli celebrates with the trophy on the podium after winning the US GP.Photograph: Mike Segar/ReutersFormula One 2026Kimi Antonelli storms to US F1 GP victory but is made to wait for title gloryChampionship leader wins from Leclerc and Verstappen20-year-old should win title in next race in MexicoGiles Richardsat the Circuit of the AmericasSun 25 Oct 2026 18.21 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 19.56 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWith a calm assurance that belies his tender years,Kimi Antonellidelivered another masterclass at the US Grand Prix, ensuring that while he could not quite seal the Formula One world championship in the Texas sunshine, it is a coronation that is surely only delayed for a week. The 20-year-old has made it almost a formality that he will seal the deal at the next round in Mexico.Antonelli’s dominant victory in Austin at the Circuit of the Americas, with a controlled and composed drive to beat the Ferrari ofCharles Leclercinto second place and the Red Bull of Max Verstappen into third, was described by the Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff as “one small step” towards the title in what has been a season of giant leaps for the Italian.Kimi Antonelli looks forward to drivers’ title after victory in US Grand PrixRead moreThose leaps were exemplified by Antonelli’s run in Austin where he did everything required of him,taking poleand converting it to a dominant race win, his ninth of the season. “The race of a champion who isn’t the champion yet,” was Wolff’s accurate assessment.Quick GuideUS GP resultsShow1Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes1:35:16.650 –25pts2Charles Leclerc🇲🇨Ferrari+13.078 –18pts3Max Verstappen🇳🇱Red Bull+17.485 –15pts4Lewis Hamilton🇬🇧Ferrari+18.515 –12pts5Lando Norris🇬🇧McLaren+30.521 –10pts6Isack Hadjar🇫🇷Red Bull+34.373 –8pts7Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren+52.674 –6pts8George Russell🇬🇧Mercedes+54.303 –4pts9Liam Lawson🇳🇿Red Bull+79.183 –2pts10Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine+87.516–1pt11Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi+94.945s12Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls+1 lap13Gabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷Audi+1 lap14Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas+1 lap15Lance Stroll🇨🇦Aston Martin+1 lap16Fernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston Martin+1 lap17Alexander Albon🇹🇭Williams+1 lap18Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams+1 lap19Sergio Pérez🇲🇽Cadillac+1 lapNCValtteri Bottas🇫🇮Cadillac+1 lapNCFranco Colapinto🇦🇷AlpineDNFNCOliver Bearman🇬🇧HaasDNFWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.However, while it was a perfect weekend for the Italian, it was not quite enough to claim the title in Texas. With his teammate George Russell finishing in eighth place andLewis Hamiltonin fourth for Ferrari, the fight remains alive but only just and Antonelli is now in position to finish the job next weekend in Mexico City.Antonelli leads Russell by 123 points and Hamilton by 124. With nine wins, the Italian cannot be caught on countback and needs to be only 100 ahead after the Mexican GP. Any finish in front of Russell and Hamilton, or ninth or better regardless of where his two rivals finish, will be enough for him to become the youngest driver to claim the sport’s crown and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari in 1953. The joy when Antonelli climbed from the car was palpable as he allowed himself the chance to acknowledge the feeling that he really is now world champion-elect.View image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli doused himself in the winner’s champagne and knows ninth or better in Mexico will suffice for him to be world champion.Photograph: Jerome Miron/Imagn Images/ReutersIt was not a thrilling victory in what was something of a stately affair, but again Antonelli had its measure and was all but untouchable in a race enlivened really only by a split strategy.The Mercedes of Antonelli and Russell opted for a one-stop strategy over the two-stop choice ofRed Bulland Ferrari, and the former proved to be the right call. Antonelli led from the off and after putting in a long first stint while his rivals dashed in for new boots, he emerged able to regain the lead without having to stop again.The strategy split made the procession at least open to debate for the mid-period until it became clear that the one-stop option was the quicker. The late phase did see some feisty passing by Verstappen, who took advantage of his fresher rubber to hustle through the field, as in his wake did Leclerc, who was equally brave and ultimately took second place. Verstappen finished in third, although he was suffering with engine-braking problems. Hamilton, too, made a late pass to claim fourth , with Lando Norris in fifth for McLarenThe race belonged to Antonelli, however. He did not put a foot wrong with a cool-headed display as he assuredly put one hand on the title. The Italianwent into the weekend insistinghe just wanted to have fun, to perform at his best and without letting the title play on his mind. He did so with no little success.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe pole lap had been brilliant, his first since Belgium in July, and in the race he demonstrated the same imperious form as when at his very best this season and which has brought him to within touching distance of his record-breaking achievement.Quick GuideHow the title races standShowDrivers' standings1Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes365pts2George Russell 🇬🇧Mercedes2423Lewis Hamilton 🇬🇧Ferrari2414Max Verstappen 🇳🇱Red Bull2365Charles Leclerc 🇲🇨Ferrari2336Lando Norris 🇬🇧McLaren2117Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren1448Isack Hadjar🇫🇷Red Bull1059Liam Lawson🇳🇿Racing Bulls7710Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine4211Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls3812Franco Colapinto🇦🇷Alpine2713Oliver Bearman 🇬🇧Haas2314Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi1315Gabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷Audi1016Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas717Fernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston Martin718Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams719Alexander Albon🇹🇭Williams520Yuki Tsunoda🇯🇵Racing Bulls1Yet to score:Lance Stroll🇨🇦Aston MartinValtteri Bottas🇫🇮CadillacSergio Pérez🇲🇽CadillacConstructors' standings1Mercedes🇩🇪 607pts2Ferrari🇮🇹 4743Red Bull🇦🇹 3554McLaren🇬🇧3555Racing Bulls🇮🇹 1026Alpine🇫🇷 697Haas🇺🇸 308Audi🇩🇪 239Williams🇬🇧1210Aston Martin🇬🇧711Cadillac🇺🇸 0Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Just as his five-race run of victories at the start of the season had given him command of the title fight, he is closing it out with nerveless control. The pole, he admitted, had been something of a surprise given how strong Red Bull have been of late but the victory was an emphatic reminder that these are the performances Antonelli is always capable of delivering.Moreover, the result was welcomed with open arms at Mercedes. The minor wobble they experienced when their upgrades brought to Malaysiadid not deliver as expectedand left the team having to work at bringing the package up to speed, looks to be over. The upgrade is not where they want it to be, the car’s operating window is narrower, but they have a handle on it that the victory demonstrated even if, as Wolff noted, the car remains unsuited to Russell’s style.That is particularly true in comparison to Antonelli, in whose hands the Mercedes once more looked like it was on rails. He went into this race needing to win and he delivered, ensuring that the title race is all over bar the shouting.Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Motor sportFormula OneKimi AntonelliMercedes GPGeorge RussellLewis HamiltonnewsShareReuse this content

title: The WNBA finals are a basketball wonderland – unless you’re part of the Maga machine | WNBA | The Guardian
description: The Dream and Valkyries are tied at 2-2 after four absorbing games. Many in America would rather we revisited the national anthem debate
Author: Andrew Lawrence
Headline: The Dream and Valkyries are tied at 2-2 after four absorbing games. Many in America would rather we revisited the national anthem debate
Content: Angel Reese and the Dream are tied 2-2 with the Valkyries in the WNBA finals.Photograph: Brynn Anderson/APView image in fullscreenAngel Reese and the Dream are tied 2-2 with the Valkyries in the WNBA finals.Photograph: Brynn Anderson/APWNBAThe WNBA finals are a basketball wonderland – unless you’re part of the Maga machineThe Dream and Valkyries are tied at 2-2 after four absorbing games. Many in America would rather we revisited the national anthem debateAndrew Lawrenceat State Farm ArenaSun 25 Oct 2026 08.48 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 10.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhen Tyler Perry leading lady Crystal Renee took center stage at State Farm Arena to sing the national anthem before the Atlanta Dream’s WNBA finals clash with the Golden State Valkyries on Saturday afternoon, a smattering of photographers, game officials and event security took their familiar places around her as the capacity crowd stood for the flag. The teams, as is now customary, spent that time in their locker rooms. As soon as the lights went back up, the teams returned to the floor to resume their shootarounds. Anyone genuinely invested in the finals would have been unfazed by them briefly stepping away – if they remembered it at all afterthe Valkyries’ 67-62 wintied the series at two games apiece. But for many watching the game, basketball is beside the point.Seven years ago, Jay-Z declared that the culture had “moved past kneeling” and similar national anthem protests, seemingly sounding the death knell for an era of sports activism that had helped raise awareness of racial disparities as a broader social movement gathered force. The line cemented his partnership with the NFL as the league bowed to political pressure to crack down on anthem protests, with other major US sports eventually following the NFL’s lead. But rightwing media and politicians never got the memo. They’re still making sports a battleground for patriotism, with basketball as the war’s chief casualty.Quick GuideWNBA finals 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times Eastern.Sat 17 OctGame 1:Golden State 68, Atlanta 64Mon 19 OctGame 2:Atlanta 79, Golden State 65Wed 21 OctGame 3:Atlanta 97, Golden State 71Sat 24 OctGame 4:Golden State 67, Atlanta 62Mon 26 OctGame 5: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Thu 29 OctGame 6: Golden State at Atlanta, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, the series will air on NBC, USA Network and CNBC, with all games streaming on Peacock. In the UK, it will be carried by Sky Sports. In Australia, fans can watch through WNBA League Pass, with selected coverage also available through ESPN.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Credit OutKick, Fox’s renegade sports arm, for providing the spark that reignited the right’s outrage machine. They tipped off theWNBAfinals by making a story out of Atlanta and Golden State leaving the court during the national anthem, then amplified the indignation aimed at LeBron James for appearing to practice his golf swing during the anthem at a Philadelphia 76ers game that same week.Valkyries hold off Dream comeback to win Game 4 and level WNBA finals at 2-2Read moreThat was all the scene-setting Donald Trump needed. “You know the NFL did that for a while and they stopped because people stopped watching games. I think you should do the same thing with women’s basketball,” Trump said. In a Truth Social post,he called James a “disgrace”and demanded he “apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!”Basketball has grown accustomed to this kind of punching down from the White House and the familiar cycle of provocation and outrage, especially whenthe administration’s poll numbers are dragging.James dismissedTrump’s diss as a sign of a “slow news day at the office” and the WNBA declined to engage, beyond noting that players haven’t been on court for the anthem for years now. Meanwhile, the Dream and Valkyries have been too preoccupied with winning their first championship to really enter the chat.“For me, it’s staying off social media. It’s just going inward with our teammates and staff,” said veteran Golden State center Kiah Stokes, who helped drive her team’s victory with her stout defense of Atlanta star Angel Reese. “Staying together. That’s been one of our keys all season.”But no matter how hard the WNBA resists the urge to clap back, no matter how valiantly it tries to keep the spotlight on basketball, there will always be someone on the right looking to steal it for their grievance grift. As OutKick and Trump reheated the stale anthem controversy,former NBA player turned Maga wannabeEnes Kanter Freedom was making a grand show of his latest appearance at a WNBA game,asking for special security arrangementsso he could watch Game 3 of the finals from a courtside seat. The Dream offered to accommodate Kanter Freedom –who has disrupted WNBA games in the past– with a fully stocked suite, courtesy of the team and State Farm. But Kanter Freedom refused and beat a retreatwith his camera crew.Jennifer Sey, the red-pilled former US gymnastics champion, has attended this year’s finals in her anti-trans athletic gear – and her efforts to incite a reaction from the W’s progressives went largely unnoticed, too.It is unfortunate that these finals have become a microcosm of the WNBA season,a tug-of-warbetween a basketball product that has never been better and a political class desperate to bend it to its own agenda. But the longer the right keeps up its fight, the more it gives its game away – exposing the hypocrisy beneath its moral posturing. We’ve seen how urgently conservative culture warriors believe women need protecting when the alleged assailant isn’t transgender. “Cornell’s a fine school,” Trump said in response to the university’s handling of a student’s gang-rape allegations. “I’m sure they’ll do what’s right.” We’ve seen how much this administration cares about its great American heroes as it sends them into an open-ended conflict, keeps sailors at sea forrecord stretchesanddownplays casualties, injuries and damage to US assetsin the war with Iran – all while slashing veterans’ jobs across the federal government.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWe know why basketball makes such a ripe target for attacks from Maga’s crusaders of the American way: the game’s politics lean left, its players are well-traveled, culturally sensitive and have no qualms aboutdunking on trolls. And we know why the WNBA, in particular, gets under the right’s skin: it issoBlack and queer, and its players haveset the tonefor political protest in American sports. The Dream, specifically,helped usherRaphael Warnock, the Atlanta pastor whodelivers sermons from Martin Luther King Jr’s pulpit, into the US Senate.We see the play Kanter Freedom is trying to run by seeking out an altercation with a player in front of Atlanta’s largely African American crowd, and the statement Sey hopes to make by swanning around queer-friendly Ballhalla in her statementware. We see how closely these grifters actually follow women’s sports. That much was clear again in a recent episode of The Georgia Gang, Atlanta’s long-running political TV roundtable, when the talk turned to the home town team’s WNBA finals berth. “Go Sophie Cunningham, she my’s girl not Angel Reese,” said panelist Phil Kent, a conservative consultant – a contrarian move that also betrayed his refusal to appreciate the absorbing WNBA finals matchup we are being treated to: Maga It girl Cunningham and her Indiana Fever crashed out in the first round. When others at the roundtable praised Reese’s selection as defensive player of the year, Kent doubled down (“I question that”) – andthe cliphas since drawn a torrent of criticism. “These white men are so broken,” said one Twitter user. “It’s never been about basketball.”The Valkyries enter Game 5 with momentum on their side (“Block out the noise and understand the gameplan” was coach Natalie Nakase’s recipe for victory on Monday), but how the rest of the series unfolds is anyone’s guess. Will Stokes keep holding Reese in check? Will the Dream be forced back intotheir rinky-dink home arenafor Game 6? Will the series go the distance and breakmore ratings records? The storylines are almost too juicy – and they’re the last thing anyone on the right will want to talk about.Explore more on these topicsWNBAGolden State ValkyriesAtlanta DreamBasketballUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller  | La Liga | The Guardian
description: The French forward scored in the 41st and 87th minute as Real Madrid closed the gap on the La Liga leaders Barcelona with a 2-1 win
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: The French forward scored in the 41st and 87th minute as Real Madrid closed the gap on the La Liga leaders Barcelona with a 2-1 win
Content: Kylian Mbappé is all smiles after scoring Real Madrid’s 87th-minute winner.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersView image in fullscreenKylian Mbappé is all smiles after scoring Real Madrid’s 87th-minute winner.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersLa LigaMbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha levellerSid Loweat the Camp NouSun 25 Oct 2026 18.12 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 19.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThirteen years later, José Mourinho ledReal Madridinto the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written.“The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again.Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: El Clásico – live reactionRead moreIn the corner, Madrid’s players piled on. This was the Frenchman’s 10th goal against Barcelona butnone felt quite like this. Not only was this the first time Barcelona failed to win in the league this season, their record-equalling run halted at nine; it was the first time they had failed to win any game since returning here a year ago.“I’m not going to let them have their heads on the moon,” Mourinho said, but he knew what this meant. So much for a struggling side heading to an inevitable fall; so much forBarcelonagoing nine points clear, the title race run before November. There is life in Madrid and in this league. Life in their manager too: this was expertly planned and executed, the rivals who were running at 4.3 goals per game reduced to just one. Those certainties, misplaced, seemed a long way away now; a season starts here instead.In the beginning, the ball was all Barcelona’s but no sooner had they lost it than the first shot was Madrid’s, Pedri’s startlingly loose pass allowing Arda Guler to break and fire over on four minutes. That felt like a pattern set, a portrait of the way both teams would likely approach this. So too did the way that Marc Cucurella went for Lamine Yamal, the Madrid full-back seeking a way under the winger’s skin – a task in which, it had to be ­concluded, he was successful.View image in fullscreenRaphinha is congratulated by his teammates after scoring Barcelona’s equaliser.Photograph: Jose Breton/APThe impression though was deceptive, Madrid willing to step on to the front foot and apply a pressure with which Barcelona were not comfortable, Pedri and Rodri unable to fully settle. Where they could they played too, Bernardo Silva included alongside Aurélien Tchouaméni.They were also, naturally enough, ready to run. In those early phases, Fede Valverde was opening the pitch with long diagonals. From one, Mbappé went dashing up the left, leading to Joan García scooping away ­Guler’s shot. This was frantic and Madrid were finding it to their liking, Mbappé and Yan Diomandé a threat.Quick GuideEuropean football roundupShowBallon d’Or contender Harry Kane failed to find the net on Sunday, butBayernMunichwon 3-1 away atFreiburgto regain top spot in the Bundesliga.The visitors took a 2-0 lead through Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry — his 100th goal in the Bundesliga — before an 82nd-minute Tom Bischof own goal brought Freiburg back into the contest, but Michael Olise secured victory for Bayern in the fifth minute of added time.Bayern remain without their head coach, Vincent Kompany, who collapsed during training on Friday, but lead the Bundesliga on goal difference fromBorussia Dortmund, who beatEintracht Frankfurt1-0 on Saturday.Marcus Thuram scored and then earned the penalty  that decidedInter’s late, come-from-behind 2-1 victory over visitingFiorentina.Álex Jiménez had put Fiorentina ahead midway through the second half at San Siro. Thuram equalised in the first minute of added time with a low shot through traffic and  was tugged down minutes later to set up a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the seventh minute of stoppage time.That late comeback  moved Inter back to the top of the table, level on 22 points with Lazio but ahead on goal difference.Juventuseased pastLeccein Serie A, with first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz enough to secure a 2-0 victory.It was only Juve's second win in six league outings, an inconsistent run of early season form that sees Luciano Spalletti's just outside the European places in Italy.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The hosts tried to impose control but could not. That said, they too enjoy flying into space, and from a Pedri run Raphinha shot over. Then Anthony Gordon bombed through and produced a neat back-heel for Raphinha to curl wide. The Brazilian would have another shot wide soon after, although the openings were often lost to an insistence on playing (and ­wasting) one last pass or, conversely, to snatch at shots. The half’s best opportunity came when Guler’s gorgeous ball was volleyed over by Mbappé. Back and forth it went, Gordon drawing a sharp save from Andriy Lunin.In the midst of it all the Camp Nou roared in indignation with each, increasingly intense Cucurella challenge on Lamine Yamal, before silence fell on 41 minutes. Cucurella released Diomandé, so often the destination, who pulled across low and hard. Gerard Martín got there first but could only hit it against Mbappé and in. There was fortune there, but it had been worked for, not simply found. And when Lamine Yamal had a wonderful chance to level he wasted the opportunity, scuffing wide at the near post, a picture of a night that wasn’t his.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOlder, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásicoRead moreBarcelona came back at Madrid in the second half. The tackles around the box were racking up: Tchouaméni and Bellingham, Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté. The threat never went away, Martín ended one ­Bellingham break, but the match had tilted. On the hour Barcelona were level. Lamine Yamal took a corner short to Pedri who slipped a clever angled, reversed ball into Raphinha to strike low into the net.The noise rose. Raphinha was denied at one end. García saved from Guler at the other. And, Barcelona back again, Lunin made an astonishing stop from Martín’s header. Barcelona had taken a grip but not entirely, leaving them exposed to every break and leaving the game, the players and the entire place on edge. Mbappé ran at Barcelona, Pedri ran back again, leading a move that concluded with some neat footwork and a shot just wide. Huijsen then dived in to stop Frenkie de Jong and stopped a Lamine Yamal shot with his face, laying him out. The chance had been laid on by Gordon.Barcelona insisted. Madrid, tired now, resisted. But there was still some fight in them, and still some finish too.Explore more on these topicsLa LigaBarcelonaReal MadridEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Jokić says booing fans ‘not welcome’ after Nuggets rally from 23 points down to beat Pelicans | NBA | The Guardian
description: Nikola Jokić scored eight of his 35 points in overtime and finished with 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and short-handed Denver rallied from 23 points down
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Nikola Jokić scored eight of his 35 points in overtime and finished with 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and short-handed Denver rallied from 23 points down
Content: Nikola Jokić registered his 199th career triple-double.Photograph: David Zalubowski/APView image in fullscreenNikola Jokić registered his 199th career triple-double.Photograph: David Zalubowski/APNBAJokić says booing fans ‘not welcome’ after Nuggets rally from 23 points down to beat PelicansNew Orleans Pelicans 135-141 Denver Nuggets (OT)Nuggets fans showed displeasure at half-timeAgenciesSun 25 Oct 2026 07.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNikola Jokić scored eight of his 35 points in overtime and finished with 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the short-handed Denver Nuggets rallied from 23 points down to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 on Saturday night.Jokić had his 199th career triple-double in the regular season, second to Russell Westbrook, who retired with 209.Sections of the Nuggets home crowd booed the team when they went into half-time 73-57 down. After the game, Jokić made his displeasure clear.“We got booed at our first home game, and I think those fans who booed us, they don’t need to come anymore,” Jokić said. “If you guys follow us, you know that we never quit and we’ve come back from much worse situations. So, if they ask me, they are not welcome anymore.”Jamal Murray scored 42 points and rookie Trevon Brazille had seven of his 17 points in overtime in his home debut for Denver, which took an early lead in overtime. His corner three-pointer with 1:25 left in overtime gave the Nuggets a 133-129 lead.Denver played without Cam Johnson (ankle) and Alpha Diallo (sprained wrist) and continued to be without Julian Strawther and Spencer Jones.Trey Murphy III led New Orleans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22 points and Derik Queen and Zion Williamson scored 17 each. The Pelicans have dropped their first three games under first-year coach Jamahl Mosley.New Orleans shot 65.9% in the first half and led by 23. Denver rallied to cut it to 16, and Jokić and Murray combined to score 22 of the Nuggets’ 32 points in the third quarter but the Pelicans extended the lead to 19 heading into the fourth.Denver erased the deficit on three-pointers from Murray and Jokić, a reverse dunk from Aaron Gordon, and then had a chance to go ahead with 17 seconds left but Murray made two of three free throws to tie it.Explore more on these topicsNBANikola JokićBasketballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Brewers erase four-run deficit to stun Rays and take 2-0 World Series lead | World Series | The Guardian
description: Sal Frelick and Cooper Pratt sparked another Milwaukee comeback as the Brewers overturned a four-run deficit to move two wins from a World Series title
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Sal Frelick and Cooper Pratt sparked another Milwaukee comeback as the Brewers overturned a four-run deficit to move two wins from a World Series title
Content: Milwaukee’s Sal Frelick rounds the bases after hitting a game-tying solo home run in the sixth inning against Tampa Bay during Game 2 of the World Series.Photograph: Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMilwaukee’s Sal Frelick rounds the bases after hitting a game-tying solo home run in the sixth inning against Tampa Bay during Game 2 of the World Series.Photograph: Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos/Getty ImagesWorld SeriesBrewers erase four-run deficit to stun Rays and take 2-0 World Series leadMilwaukee rally from 4-0 down to win 5-4 in Game 2Frelick homers before Pratt delivers go-ahead singleRays undone by defensive mistakes in seventh inningAgenciesSun 25 Oct 2026 00.12 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 00.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSal Frelick tied the score with his first home run in three months, Cooper Pratt hit a go-ahead single in the seventh inning and theMilwaukee Brewersstunned the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 on Saturday night for a 2-0 World Series lead by overcoming a four-run deficit for the second time in the postseason.Tampa Bay, who won the AL pennant by forcing opponents into mistakes, committed one error, made two other misplays that could have been charged as errors and had a runner thrown out at the plate.The World Series of the have-nots is here.
