But baseball’s money problem isn’t going away | Tom DartRead moreDown 4-0 in the first inning, Milwaukee rallied for their seventh comeback win of this postseason. The Brewers also rebounded from a 4-0 deficit to beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the NL Championship Series, completing a four-game sweep.After losing Friday’s opener 3-2, the Rays burst ahead against rookie Logan Henderson but the Brewers started to claw back with two runs in the bottom half against Tampa Bay ace Drew Rasmussen.David Hamilton cut the deficit to 4-3 with a run-scoring grounder in the fourth and Frelick capped a nine-pitch at-bat against Ian Seymour in the sixth by driving a fastball over the center-field fence.Quick GuideWorld Series 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times US Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).Sat 17 OctGame 1:Golden State 68, Atlanta 64Mon 19 OctGame 2:Atlanta 79, Golden State 65Wed 21 OctGame 3:Atlanta 97, Golden State 71Sat 24 OctGame 4:Golden State 67, Atlanta 62Mon 26 OctGame 5: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Thu 29 OctGame 6: Golden State at Atlanta, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, all World Series games will air on Fox and Fox Deportes, with streaming available through Fox One. In the UK, the series will be carried by TNT Sports. In Australia, fans can watch on ESPN, with streaming available through Disney+ and Kayo Sports.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Frelick had gone 103 plate appearances without a home run since his 11 July drive off Pittsburgh’s Braxton Ashcraft and had not gone deep against a left-handed pitcher since opening day against Tyler Gilbert of the Chicago White Sox. Frelick sped around the bases in 18.72 seconds, half the time of some theatrical trots this postseason.Screaming fans at the second game of Milwaukee’s firstWorld Seriessince 1982 were fired up during the seventh-inning stretch, dancing to the Beer Barrel Polka played by Mike Schneider, an accordionist from Clinton, Wisconsin.Brice Turang doubled against losing pitcher Tyler Wells on the second pitch of the bottom half, advanced on Garrett Mitchell’s flyout to right and scored when Pratt, a 22-year-old who debuted in June, looped a sinker from Kevin Kelly into short right field.Abner Uribe pitched one and one-third hitless innings for the win.Jonny DeLuca doubled off Aaron Ashby starting the ninth, then Victor Mesa Jr struck out when he couldn’t check his swing. Pinch-hitter Ben Williamson’s groundout advanced the runner and Yandy Díaz struck out when he couldn’t check his swing on a full-count pitch.Ashby has three saves in the postseason while not allowing a run.Milwaukee won their seventh straight game, becoming the fifth team to twice overcome four-run deficits for victories in a single postseason and the first since Philadelphia in 2022.Game 3 of the matchup between teams seeking their first title is Monday night at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Florida, where the Brewers last played in 2023.Of the 57 previous teams to take 2-0 World Series leads, 46 claimed the championship.Tampa Bay took a 4-2 lead in the highest-scoring Series first inning since Game 4 in 1993 as the teams combined for seven hits, tying the most in an opening frame.View image in fullscreenBrewers catcher William Contreras celebrates as the Rays’ Yandy Díaz reacts after striking out to end Game 2 of the World Series on Saturday in Milwaukee.Photograph: David J Phillip/APStill, Milwaukee improved to 13-0 in games started by Henderson, dating to his 2025 debut. He followed Jacob Misiorowski in the Brewers’ rotation, the first time teammates aged 24 or younger started the first two games of the Series since Cincinnati’s Gary Nolan and Ross Grimsley in 1972.Henderson started on 11 days’ rest and struggled as the Rays fouled off 13 of 35 pitches in the first. He gave up four runs – three earned – in three innings.Given an extra day of rest, Rasmussen allowed three runs and six hits over three and two-thirds innings in his shortest start since 9 July.Pratt made his fourth error of the postseason at shortstop, the Brewers’ ninth in 10 games, bouncing his throw past first baseman Jake Bauers on a leadoff grounder by Díaz. Chandler Simpson and Junior Caminero followed with RBI singles, and Liam Hicks hit a two-run homer.Jackson Chourio and Bauers started the bottom half with singles and first baseman Jonathan Aranda allowed Contreras’ one-out foul pop to bounce out of his mitt near netting in front of the seats.With Bauers running on a full-count pitch, Contreras bounced an RBI single to the left of second baseman Richie Palacios, who had taken a step toward the base. Mitchell’s two-out single cut the deficit to 4-2.Hamilton hit an RBI grounder in the fourth that bounced under Aranda’s legs for an error.Chourio threw out Hicks from left for the final out of the sixth when third base coach Brady Williams waved the slow-footed catcher to try to score from second on Mesa’s single.Explore more on these topicsWorld SeriesMilwaukee BrewersTampa Bay RaysBaseballUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Alexander Isak was on target again as Liverpool ended Brighton’s four-game winning run in the league with a 2-0 victory at Anfield
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Alexander Isak was on target again as Liverpool ended Brighton’s four-game winning run in the league with a 2-0 victory at Anfield
Content: Alexander Isak is congratulated by teammates after scoring Liverpool’s second goal.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAView image in fullscreenAlexander Isak is congratulated by teammates after scoring Liverpool’s second goal.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAPremier LeagueIsak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an endAndy Hunterat AnfieldSun 25 Oct 2026 12.12 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBrighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in thePremier Leaguethis season, who looked upwardly mobile.There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially creditedto Brighton’s Pascal Grossand Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break.Manchester United 0-3 Bournemouth, Liverpool 2-0 Brighton and more: clockwatch – as it happenedRead moreFabian Hürzeler praised the Brighton performance and the self-belief necessary to take the game toLiverpoolwhen trailing to two quickfire goals. But he exaggerated the threat they displayed. Yasin Ayari missed a glorious chance to open the scoring and also struck a post, but Alisson was troubled more by his own distribution after Liverpool’s second goal than by anything the visitors engineered.“I think everyone in the stadium saw there was one team who really tried to create and tried to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” claimed the Brighton head coach, prompting a mass raising of eyebrows in the post-match press conference. “The difference was that they scored and we didn’t. They blocked a lot of shots and defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes and lost some important personal duels but overall I saw a team with a lot of good things. It is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”Storm Boelo raged outside the stadium but inside it was relatively calm, vindicating the decision to proceed with the game. But not for Brighton. Liverpool’s attacking force devastated the visitors’ hopes of a fifth straight win and clean sheet in succession in the Premier League. The hosts were aggressive and sharp from the start, in contrast to their opening against Villarreal in the Champions League, and opened the scoring just as Brighton were beginning to exert their first serious spell of pressure.There was an element of good fortune about the breakthrough but it also encapsulated the differing intensity between the teams when Wirtz held off Lewis Dunk and Araújo beat the Brighton captain and Olivier Boscagli to the loose ball. His low cross rebounded off two Brighton players before going to Wirtz, whose first-time shot deceived Bart Verbruggen via another deflection off Gross. Wirtz’s low-key celebration hinted at what was to come. It was not his first league goal of the campaign and second goal in successive games after all. The breakthrough was officially credited as an own goal from the Brighton midfielder.View image in fullscreenFlorian Wirtz’s shot was credited as an own goal by his fellow German, Pascal Gross.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAIt should also have been a Liverpool equaliser rather than the opener. Diego Gómez and Gross combined to pierce Liverpool’s left flank and present Ayari with a free sight of goal with Alisson dragged across to his left. The Brighton forward blazed high into the Kop and would soon have added reason to rue the miscue.Liverpool soon doubled their lead when capitalising on more casual Brighton defending. Boscagli was again found wanting when attempting to deal with Alisson’s clearance. The left-back struck a clearance straight at Barcola and was left floundering as the France international, deployed on the right, brushed aside his efforts to recover possession. Isak steered Barcola’s delivery inside the far corner with a deft, side-foot finish to score in three consecutive league games for the first time since January 2025. There was no surprise whatsoever when Boscagli was withdrawn at half-time.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBrighton attacked with greater conviction than they defended but with Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk making telling interventions, and receiving impressive support from all quarters, Alisson was not seriously extended. The visitors’ best hope of a recovery stemmed from the Liverpool keeper’s own risky pass to Alexis Mac Allister, which gifted possession back to Brighton and resulted in Ayari striking a post from 20 yards out.Jack Hinshelwood, Boscagli’s replacement, and fellow substitute Malick Yalcouyé injected more energy and bite into Brighton’s second-half display but an end product from the visitors remained lacking. Too many overhit crosses and poor final balls enabled Liverpool to protect their lead in comfort.Iraola said: “It is a very valuable win. The key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions, and we’ve done it and it has been a different game from the last oneswhen we’ve conceded first.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueLiverpoolBrighton & Hove Albionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Manchester United’s Elisabeth Terland struck an 89th-minute equaliser to cancel out Khadija Shaw’s goal and earn a 1-1 draw against Manchester City
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Manchester United’s Elisabeth Terland struck an 89th-minute equaliser to cancel out Khadija Shaw’s goal and earn a 1-1 draw against Manchester City
Content: Elisabeth Terland thrashes home the loose ball to secure a point for Manchester United against their city rivals.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenElisabeth Terland thrashes home the loose ball to secure a point for Manchester United against their city rivals.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersWomen's Super LeagueTerland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSLTom Garryat the Progress With Unity StadiumSun 25 Oct 2026 16.38 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 19.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby.Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher.Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSLRead moreHowever, Eva Olid’s ever-improving hosts fought back and were good value for the draw, which they eventually earned when Terland found the bottom corner after the ball fell kindly to her in the penalty area.Olid, in fact, repeatedly said in her post-match press conference that her side had “deserved to win”.United climbed to fourth in the table, while that late strike meant City dropped to ­second – now behind Chelsea on goal difference – and breathed fresh life and intrigue into the title race. Perhaps more strikingly, if any United fans who saw their men’s team beinghumbled by Bournemouthearlier on Sunday managed to navigate the winds of Storm Boelo and get to Leigh for this 6pm kick-off, they will have seen a team with characteristics unrecognisable from those wearing red at Old Trafford; hard work, resilience, teamwork, running – real, hard running – and fighting spirit.This United team markedly improved on last season’s league meetings with their local rivals, both of which ended in 3-0 victories for City. This time Andrée Jeglertz’s visitors were given a real test.Quick GuideWSL roundup:ShowChelseacame from behind to beatCrystal Palace3-1 after Molly Bartrip’s shock opener. It was the first time Chelsea had trailed all season and they struck back in the second half with two Melvine Malard goals, before Sandy Baltimore converted from the penalty spot in the 90th minute.London City Lionessesstayed third after drawing 2-2 atLiverpool, with the visitors denied all three points by a stoppage-time own goal from Jana Fernández. Freya Godfrey and Kadidiatou Diani had earlier wiped out Beata Olsson’s penalty.Aston Villamoved level on points withEvertonafter winning 3-2 at Goodison Park. Amalie Vangsgaard’s double put Villa three up after Noelle Maritz’s early goal, before the hosts made it a nervy finish with two late goals.Birminghamwon for the first time this season as Wilma Leidhammar’s effort midway through the second half saw offCharlton1-0.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.For spells of the first half, City’s fluid pass-and-move football, their speed down the left-wing with ­Lauren Hemp, and the technical prowess of Yui Hasegawa and Aoba Fujino in particular, made it feel as though there was only one likely outcome, as Fujino fizzed an effort narrowly wide of the United goal.United, though, proved a tough nut to crack and, against the run of play, created the better chances of the opening 45 minutes.Terland was unable to reset her feet and ­connect properly with Andrea Medina’s ­cutback. Later Ella Toone and Jess Park both had efforts saved by Ayaka Yamashita.View image in fullscreenKhadija Shaw blasts Manchester City into the lead against United.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersPark’s powerful, driven shot clipped the top of the crossbar around the hour mark, after Yamashita had saved well from Terland one-on-one.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNot long later, though, last season’s WSL Golden Boot winner Shaw ­delivered the breakthrough with a ruthless, low strike that was hit with too much venom for Phallon ­Tullis-Joyce to react. Shaw, who had been booed by the home fans after exchanging robust challenges with Maya Le Tissier in the first half, ran across to celebrate in front of the City fans, many of whom were waving inflatable bananas in the air. She almost had a second goal moments later but whipped a close-range, rising shot just over the bar.Shaw glanced a header wide from a City corner and Grace Clinton missed a huge chance to seal it for the ­visitors. Continuing to battle, United were eventually rewarded when Le Tissier’s hopeful, high ball into the box, after a free-kick was taken short, was met by a defensive header from Shaw, but that only dropped as far as Terland who lashed in first time to draw huge roars and clenched fists from the United technical area.Jeglertz is staying calm, insisting: “Nothing has changed. We are absolutely on the right track, in everything we are doing. We are playing well in most of the games and getting the result in most of the games. But this league is challenging. [We are just going] to stay calm and focusing on the next task.”As for United, this late goal felt like a pivotal moment for Olid, giving the club a lift. Her tenure began with chastening losses to London City and Chelsea but this rally against their neighbours showed they are rapidly improving. She said: “That was one of our best performances, in general, in terms of fight, hard work, how we were ­pressing and how we played with the ball.“How this team has built in confidence from day one to now, in a short period of time – just two months and a half working together – the progression has been massive.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueManchester United WomenManchester City WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager | Crystal Palace | The Guardian
description: Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage said losing concentration for 15 minutes had cause his side’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage said losing concentration for 15 minutes had cause his side’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle
Content: Pierre Sage consoles Yéremy Pino after the final whistle.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenPierre Sage consoles Yéremy Pino after the final whistle.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianCrystal PalacePierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace managerSage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’Jonathan Wilsonat Selhurst ParkSun 25 Oct 2026 14.17 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration forCrystal Palace’s 2-0 defeatby Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.”Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in thePremier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said.Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstartRead more“My way, my idea, is that the best way to defend is to have the ball.” The problem with that is that only the three promoted sides have had less possession than Palace. “Here every mistake, every situation that is bad for the team will be a goal,” Sage said.Palace conceded two goals against Besiktas on Thursday to the only shots on target they conceded. Newcastle similarly scored with both their shots on target. “We conceded fewer chances with our defending in open play today but it’s not enough,” the Palace manager said. “For the moment the pressure is always the same because I don’t find the solution. Today was not a tactical problem but a mental problem. When we came back from the dressing room we let our opponents have too many things. When you don’t control the ball you give the initiative to the opposition.”Sage is sure he can improve ­Palace’s fortunes – they are 17th having lost back-to-back Premier League games, the other being a 5-0 thrashing by their rivals Brighton – and said that although he remains in regular contact with the Palace chair, Steve Parish, the issue of his future has never been raised. “Inside, we are just really focused on solutions,” Sage said. “How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work. There’s no noise inside, if you want.”There was relief for Matthias Jaissle as he oversaw a first ­Newcastle win in three games. “It was a tough game especially in first half,” the ­German said. “We couldn’t get ourselves the reward for the intensity of our possession.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“The first half out of possession was not that bad but we didn’t have our attacking mindset. The second half was much better. Even if you don’t play a fantastic game in possession, keeping a clean sheet is the fundamental of football.”Explore more on these topicsCrystal PalacePremier LeagueNewcastle UnitednewsShareReuse this content

title: Ouattara rescues point for Brentford as Hull maintain unbeaten home record | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Dango Ouattara’s second-half goal earned Brentford a 1-1 draw at the MKM Stadium after Oli McBurnie had put Hull ahead from the penalty spot
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Dango Ouattara’s second-half goal earned Brentford a 1-1 draw at the MKM Stadium after Oli McBurnie had put Hull ahead from the penalty spot
Content: Dango Ouattara slots in from close range to secure Brentford’s fourth consecutive away draw.Photograph: Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDango Ouattara slots in from close range to secure Brentford’s fourth consecutive away draw.Photograph: Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueOuattara rescues point for Brentford as Hull maintain unbeaten home recordPress AssociationSun 25 Oct 2026 12.40 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHull’s unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after this draw withBrentford.The opening goal came courtesy of a 24th-minute Oli McBurnie penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey flattened Tim Iroegbunam while trying to hook the ball away.Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an endRead moreAlthough Brentford’s Caoimhín Kelleher guessed right, he could not stop McBurnie scoring his firstPremier Leaguegoal for more than 900 days.After the break, Hull were left to rue some inattentive defending as Igor Thiago found his way to Dango Ouattara, who slotted the ball home under very little pressure to make it 1-1 in the 63rd minute.Jaidon Anthony pushed for a second Brentford goal and saw a shot land just wide before getting a second chance, which forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, but there was a quick counter as Mohamed Belloumi raced in the other direction before firing over from distance.An 88th-minute chance was Hull’s last opportunity to find the winning goal, but Mohamed-Ali Cho’s cross to Joe Gelhardt resulted in an off‑target shot that ensured the Tigers took no more than a point.Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, was pleased with the improved efforts of his side after thedefeat by Fulhamthe previous weekend. “I think we played a good game, especially in the first half,” he said. “We were much more aggressive in duels, we won a lot of first and second balls. Maybe there were some cheap mistakes, bad passing, bad receiving, but you see how fast they are – in five seconds they were in our box. We should have scored one or maybe two more with better decisions.”Both clubs were required to pick through the detritus of the pre-match display in the opening minutes as balloons and litter were carried by the strong winds of Storm Boelo on to the pitch.The first chance of note fell to the visitors, with Hull faltering in midfield after 11 minutes and allowing Hickey to unleash a shot that was comfortably dealt with by Tzolakis.View image in fullscreenOli McBurnie (left) hugs Mohamed Belloumi after putting Hull ahead from the penalty spot.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PATen minutes later Belloumi found McBurnie inside the box, but as the Scot was preparing to strike Mathias Jensen rushed in to foil the attempt.After 22 minutes the visitors offered their hosts a golden chance when Hickey, having failed to collect a ball from Kelleher, lunged at the legs of Iroegbunam and floored him to give away a penalty. McBurnie stepped up and made no mistake.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBrentford had to wait until the 63rd minute to equalise, Ouattara made the most of lax Hull defending to collect an Igor Thiago ball and tap home.Belloumi then reacted with a sprint towards the Brentford goal with Cho – on as a substitute – in pursuit as backup, but the long-range shot was too high and flew into the stand.The final roll of the dice was Cho’s cross in to Gelhardt, but he was wide of the mark and the whistle blew on a 1-1 draw that maintains unbeaten records home and away. Jakirovic said: “I can regret the chance we had through Mohamed-Ali Cho and Gelhardt, maybe it should have been 2-1, but in the end I think it’s a fair result.”Brentford’s head coach, Keith Andrews, who had a spell at Hull as a player, was happy to see the response from the players who were brought off the bench during the second half in the leadup to their equaliser. “It was a tough game and it was always going to be a tough game, “ he said.“I’ve got a lot of respect for Sergej and the journey he’s taken this team on – I think it’s been remarkable. We reacted well at half-time, the impact from the bench was pretty good but it was a tough game.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueHull CityBrentfordmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Roefs and Trafford stand firm as Sunderland and Leeds battle for point | Premier League | The Guardian
description: The respective goalkeepers made several key saves as Sunderland stay bottom of the Premier League after a 0-0 draw with Leeds
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: The respective goalkeepers made several key saves as Sunderland stay bottom of the Premier League after a 0-0 draw with Leeds
Content: Noah Okafor misses a late chance to secure Leeds three points.Photograph: Scott Heppell/ReutersView image in fullscreenNoah Okafor misses a late chance to secure Leeds three points.Photograph: Scott Heppell/ReutersPremier LeagueRoefs and Trafford stand firm as Sunderland and Leeds battle for pointLouise Taylorat the Stadium of LightSun 25 Oct 2026 14.46 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.54 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRégis Le Bris can usually do impassive to perfection but, by the final whistle, even Sunderland’s ultra-balanced manager was looking more than a little fed up and frustrated.His bottom-placed team had arguably just about deserved a secondPremier Leaguewin of the season but, instead, had to settle for a draw on an afternoon when the hugely disruptive Storm Boelo proved the enemy of good football.Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace managerRead moreWhile Daniel Farke will doubtless regard his resilient side’s fifth league draw of the season as a fair return on the windblown road, much now hinges on Sunderland’s visit to Coventry on Saturday.At least Le Bris’s side ended a run of four straight league defeats on a day when they could have done without meeting James Trafford’s goalkeeping excellence. “It’s so hard to win games,” said Sunderland’s manager. “But it’s a positive point; we played with intensity and togetherness. We were Sunderland today.“It’s still a long journey but I think we’ve shown we’re embracing the challenge. We probably deserved more today. But there’s no drama, no panic.”The wind was strong, and capricious enough, to bend the corner flags out of shape, send pieces of rubbish swirling around the pitch and turn passing calibration horribly awry but it would take a hurricane to throw Brian Brobbey off balance.The good news for Sunderland was that their formidable centre-forward had recovered from a hamstring injury and seemed to be relishing the physicality of his duel with Jaka Bijol.Along the way Brobbey had a ­couple of first-half chances. First came the connection with an Enzo Le Fée cross and the slightly deflected shot that prompted a decent save from Trafford.Then there was the moment when Brobbey bullied Bijol into attempting a short back-pass before charging after it and ­getting there before Trafford. Hats off to Farke’s England goalkeeper for keeping his cool, bravely ­standing his ground and eventually saving cleverly with a leg.Leeds possess a not-too shabby centre-forward of their own in ­Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He passed a late fitness test on a bruised foot and, although initially less involved than Brobbey, seemed on a mission to engage Luke O’Nien in a personal subplot.View image in fullscreenJames Trafford denies Brian Brobbey from close range.Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PAIt soon became clear that Calvert-Lewin had little enthusiasm for being marked by O’Nien’s central defensive partner, Nordi Mukiele, and duly manoeuvred himself into cameos against the former at every ­opportunity. Yet although O’Nien endured a couple of wobbles he also made a vital, quite possibly goal-preventing tackle on Calvert-Lewin as half-time beckoned.The second half had barely begun before fortune frowned on Sunderland. An attempted clearance ­concluded with O’Nien throwing out an elbow and accidentally catching Mukiele in the throat. T he former Paris Saint-Germain defender requiring lengthy treatment as Le Bris looked on anxiously.Eventually it became apparent a distressed Mukiele – who, Le Bris reported, fully recovered – could not continue and the recently erratic Omar Alderete stepped off the bench.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBy now, a generally ­second-best Leeds were renascent and it took important interceptions from Alderete and Le Fée to break the ­dangerous stride of Jayden Bogle and Ao Tanaka respectively. Undeterred, Sunderland rallied. Nilson Angulo was in encouraging form and two shots from the Ecuadorian forced Trafford into a couple of smart saves.Shortly after the hour mark the fading Brobbey was replaced by the inexperienced Ukrainian striker Timur Tutyerov as, simultaneously, Farke introduced fresh attacking legs of his own.They belonged to Noah Okafor and Anton Stach who filled the spaces behind Calvert-Lewin from where Harry Wilson and Brenden Aaronson had struggled to ­destabilise Sunderland’s backline.The game remained in the balance. Trafford did well to somehow scramble the ball to safety as Granit Xhaka’s corner very nearly curved beyond him but Robin Roefs was required to dive at Calvert-Lewin’s feet after spilling Tanaka’s shot. Calvert-Lewin wanted a penalty but Stuart Attwell disagreed and a video assistant referee check endorsed that viewpoint.When the former Newcastle midfeilder Sean Longstaff, on as a Leeds substitute, unleashed a dangerous low, 20-yard shot, Stadium of Light regulars feared the worst but Roefs proved equal to it, making a superb one-handed save to turn the ball around a post.There was still time for Longstaff to have another shot cleared off the line but Farke remained sanguine. “I’m not complaining about the draw,” said the Leeds manager. “It’s always good to have a clean sheet. It’s fair to say that, in weather like this, it wasn’t the nicest game.”Inevitably, Farke was invited to praise Trafford and his concession of a mere six league goals in eight games. “He chose a good team,” he said smiling before turning serious. “He delivers, he has the potential to be England’s No 1.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueSunderlandLeeds Unitedmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Camilo Duran scored Celtic’s winner at Easter Road as the leaders reasserted the four-pont gap over Rangers, who won on Saturday
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Camilo Duran scored Celtic’s winner at Easter Road as the leaders reasserted the four-pont gap over Rangers, who won on Saturday
Content: Camilo Durán celebrates scoring Celtic’s second goal against HibsPhotograph: Steve Welsh/PAView image in fullscreenCamilo Durán celebrates scoring Celtic’s second goal against HibsPhotograph: Steve Welsh/PAScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over HibernianHibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St JohnstoneBraga and Miller give Hearts 2-0 win at MotherwellPress AssociationSun 25 Oct 2026 13.53 EDTFirst published on Sat 24 Oct 2026 12.52 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCamilo Durán moved into double figures for the season asCelticreasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleagueredHibernian2-1 at windy Easter Road.After another Europa League setbackat home to Celta Vigoon Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break.Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s outbursts are no laughing matter for fansRead moreIt proved enough to secure a ninth win in 10 league games and ensure the recently appointed home boss, Marink Reedijk, suffered a third straight defeat since succeeding David Gray.There were a couple of blemishes forCeltic, however, as substitute Alistair Johnston’s return from injury lasted barely 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11million forward Kasper Hogh – restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches for the Hoops – again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.Derek McInnes asked hisRangersside to be “brilliant” againstSt Johnstoneand was rewarded with a 4-0 win at Ibrox on Saturday. Afterdropping two points at Dundee, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.View image in fullscreenRangers’ Kevin Kelsy scores the third goal against St Johnstone.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAMcInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”Cláudio Braga and Calvin Miller scored to helpHeartssecure a 2-0 win overMotherwellat Fir Park on Sunday. A return to winning ways after last weekend’s humbling7-1 defeat by Celticleaves Hearts four points behind second-placed Rangers and eight off the leaders. Motherwell sit 10th after this sixth straight defeat, equalling a record from 2003. They were booed off the pitch at the interval and at full time.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDundee Unitedwon a rollercoaster game 3-2 againstAberdeenat Tannadice on Saturday. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behindHearts, who are atMotherwellon Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.Two own goals helpedFalkirkclimb to seventh with a 3-0 victory overKilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header.St Mirrenended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory overDundeewith goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipRangersSt JohnstoneDundee UnitedAberdeenFalkirkKilmarnocknewsShareReuse this content

title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews | Ballon d'Or | The Guardian
description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall
Content: Veteran Blackpool inside-right, and the “Wizard of Dribble”,  Stanley Matthews (left)  in action prior to winning the inaugural Ballon d’Or in December 1956.Photograph: PAView image in fullscreenVeteran Blackpool inside-right, and the “Wizard of Dribble”,  Stanley Matthews (left)  in action prior to winning the inaugural Ballon d’Or in December 1956.Photograph: PABallon d'OrBallon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley MatthewsMatthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hallEd AaronsSun 25 Oct 2026 04.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhen football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year.A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.”Memory Lane: Ballon d’Or winners down the years – in picturesRead moreThe switch of venue to England from its usual home in Paris is a mark of respect to the man who became the first active player to receive a knighthood in 1965, a few months before retiring at the age of 50. It also provides an opportunity to recall an astonishing career that began with his local side Stoke in 1932 and made the “Wizard of Dribble” the most famous player on the planet.View image in fullscreenIn September 1956, Stanley Matthews shows his son Stanley Jr a scrapbook of cuttings from newspapers and magazines going back over 25 years of his career in football.Photograph: Popperfoto/Getty Images“He was so far ahead of his time,” says Matthews Jr, a former winner of junior Wimbledon who had a successful tennis career. “The way he trained, his football boots … they were so light, they were like slippers so that he could move quicker. Towards the end of his career, when he was back at Stoke, he had the fire brigade come and water the pitch before the game so it would be a little slick, which was better for him. Now they water the pitches all the time, you know. So he was very revolutionary in all the things he did, plus his diet and his training.”Matthews’ father, Jack, was a renowned boxer known as the Fighting Barber of Hanley and it was from him that he is said to have developed his work ethic. Matthews owned a Blackpool hotel that regularly welcomed celebrities including the comedian Charlie Chester, and was known for his early morning fitness routines on the beach that helped to prolong his career.View image in fullscreenStanley Matthews (right) visits a boot and shoe factory in 1951 where he is pictured discussing his own design with two experts.Photograph: Popperfoto/Getty ImagesHe remains the oldest Ballon d’Or winner and won the last of his 54 England caps – a number that would have been higher but for the second world war – in 1957 at the age of 42. Matthews Jr thinks his father could have lasted even longer in today’s possession-based game. “He would probably have thought: ‘My goodness, if all I had to do was pass the ball around, I could have played until I was 70,’ because a lot of the players just seem to be doing that, passing out from the back,” he says.Whereas Harry Kane and the rest of the favourites for this year’s Ballon d’Or are all multimillionaires, Matthews had to make do with at most £20 a week until the maximum wage was abolished in 1961. “We compared it to the top sportsman in the US at the time, which was [baseball player] Joe DiMaggio” says Joe Pierce, who produced the 2017 film Matthews. “He was at the height of his career, and he had just signed a contract for $100,000 a year.”View image in fullscreenStoke City’s Sir Stanley Matthews is chaired off the pitch by World Stars XI’s Lev Yashin and Ferenc Puskas as Josef Masopust (left) leads the applause for the Wizard of Dribble after his testimonial in April 1965.Photograph: Empics/PA/AlamyThat meant there were a few successful and not so successful business ventures, including his own football boot brand, hats and various books, not to mention vegetable juice. “He tried to do it in cans, but it didn’t work out,” says Pierce. “There was a problem because it went bad in the cans.”Another way of supplementing his income was coaching overseas in the off-season and between 1953 and 1978 Matthews visited an African country each summer. His love affair with the continent grew a few months after he had won the Ballon d’Or when he arrived in Ghana to play a series of exhibition matches to celebrate its independence. He was presented with an ivory sword and crowned as a “soccerhene” (soccer chief). “The King of Ghana – that’s what they called him,” says Matthews Jr. “My sister still has the stool that he was crowned on.”Matthews developed a particular affinity for South Africa. He started coaching a team in Soweto during the mid-70s who became known as Stan’s Men and secured them sponsorship from Coca-Cola before taking them to play in a tournament in Brazil. Pierce was surprised when he discovered the lengths Matthews went to under significant pressure from the apartheid government not to travel.View image in fullscreenStanley Matthews coaching in Soweto.Photograph: Courtesy of Stanley Matthews Jr“There was real drama and back and forth. The UK government was involved. The South African government was involved. There were spies involved – the South African spies at the camps and around – and he just kept pushing forward. He was good friends with the Duke of Edinburgh – they would get invited over for tea and things like that. So he had connections in high places that probably helped quite a bit.”Matthews Jr says: “He was very proud of the fact that at one stage he was banned. He said: ‘Frank Sinatra was banned as well.’ So he thought that was kind of funny. I remember him saying that the South African players had so much speed and so much talent. Dad just liked people. And he knew that they had or he thought that they had a good talent. He just wanted to see if he could help them improve.”His association with Stan’s Men ended after the 1976 Soweto Uprising, with one player in the film describing how ending contact with Matthews left a “hole in my heart”. Matthews’ death in 2000 at the age of 85 also evoked strong emotions, with more than 100,000 people turning out in Stoke for what the Guardian called the biggest public funeral since Winston Churchill.View image in fullscreenSome former members of Stan’s Men.Photograph: Courtesy of Stanley Matthews Jr“He’s probably sitting there saying: ‘I told you so,’” Pierce says of the record 78 African players in the Premier League last season. Only one African player – George Weah – and three Englishmen – Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen – have followed Matthews in winning the Ballon d’Or. Whoever is chosen this year will be following in the footsteps of one of the sport’s most celebrated figures.Explore more on these topicsBallon d'OrfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Australia’s Rebecca Henderson claims historic race walk world record | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Rebecca Henderson walked her way into the history books in Japan by becoming the first Australian track and field athlete in a generation to set a senior world record
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Rebecca Henderson walked her way into the history books in Japan by becoming the first Australian track and field athlete in a generation to set a senior world record
Content: Rebecca Henderson, pictured at the Tokyo World Athletics Championships in 2025, has broken the marathon walk world record.Photograph: Emilee Chinn/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRebecca Henderson, pictured at the Tokyo World Athletics Championships in 2025, has broken the marathon walk world record.Photograph: Emilee Chinn/Getty ImagesAthleticsAustralia’s Rebecca Henderson claims historic race walk world record25-year-old sets new global mark for race walk marathonRising star slices 19 seconds off previous record despite rainAustralian Associated PressSun 25 Oct 2026 18.44 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.47 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRebecca Henderson walked her way into the history books in Japan by becoming the first Australian track and field athlete in a generation to set a senior world record in a championship event.The rising 25-year-old from Dandenong set a new global mark for the race walk marathon – the sport’s newest championship event – clocking a remarkable three hours 14 minutes 52 seconds at the All Japan Race Walking meeting on Sunday.What’s more, the Victorian achieved the milestone while having to compete in sodden conditions on a rainy day in Takahata, in northern Japan.Former Australia sprint champion Jake Doran charged with alleged child abuseRead moreAustralian para athletes have broken global records in recent times while Olympic silver medallist Jess Hull also set the world 2000m record a couple of years ago in Monaco in a non-championship discipline.Yet Henderson’s walk was the first time in 20 years that a non-disabled athlete from the country had set a global mark in an official championship event since another Aussie race walker, Nathan Deakes, set the 50km world record on the roads of Geelong in December 2006.Henderson is a double Olympian who keeps improving, having recently won the Commonwealth Games bronze at 10,000m on the track in Glasgow after last year taking World University Games team silver in Bochum.But this was by far the biggest achievement of her career in the event which became, along with the half-marathon, a WorldAthleticsofficial race walk distance in January, replacing the traditional 20km and 35km races.The longer race over the official distance of 42.195km clearly suits the Australian, who was making her marathon debut. She had finished ninth in the 35km at last year’s world athletics championships in Tokyo.Henderson’s time, even in the atrocious conditions, still sliced 19 seconds off the previous record set by Italian Sofia Fiorini when she won the European Championships in Birmingham in August.She race-walked solo for most of the race, eventually winning the women’s race by 14 minutes while overtaking many of the men in the mixed field.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every daySign up toAustralia SportGet a daily roundup of the latest sports news, features and comment from our Australian sports deskEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThere was more Australian success in the half-marathon in Takahata as Elizabeth McMillen, who beat Henderson at the Commonwealth Games where she won silver, earned victory in 1:31:31 – the fifth-fastest time yet in the new women’s event and an Australian record, slicing almost seven minutes off her best.In a landmark double, home athlete, Japan’s Masatora Kawano, two days after his 28th birthday, also set the inaugural men’s world race walk marathon record at the same Takahata event, clocking 2:55:14.It was the same venue where Kawano also set a world record of 2:21:47 over 35km two years ago.Explore more on these topicsAthleticsAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Kimi Antonelli looks forward to drivers’ title after victory in US Grand Prix | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: The F1 champion-elect, now two points from his first championship, said: ‘Hopefully we can clinch it soon,’  but Max Verstappen was unhappy with his car
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: The F1 champion-elect, now two points from his first championship, said: ‘Hopefully we can clinch it soon,’ but Max Verstappen was unhappy with his car
Content: The world championship title remains on hold for now, but Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes still had every reason to be jubilant.Photograph: Kaylee Greenlee/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe world championship title remains on hold for now, but Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes still had every reason to be jubilant.Photograph: Kaylee Greenlee/ReutersFormula One 2026Kimi Antonelli looks forward to drivers’ title after victory in US Grand PrixF1 champion-elect: ‘Hopefully we can clinch it soon’Italian two points from title but Verstappen unhappyGiles Richardsat the Circuit of the AmericasSun 25 Oct 2026 18.33 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 20.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKimi Antonelli has acknowledged the Formula One world championship is within his grasp after the Italian took a dominant victory at the US Grand Prix which has put him just two points away from clinching his first title at the Mexican Grand Prix next weekend.Antonelli beat the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc into second place and the Red Bull of Max Verstappen into third. With his title rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton finishing eighth and fourth respectively, Antonelli will take the title if he finishes ninth or better in Mexico City.Kimi Antonelli storms to US F1 GP victory but is made to wait for title gloryRead moreThe 20-year-old, who stands to becomeFormula 1’s youngest champion, was jubilant as he crossed the line at the Circuit of the Americas. “Yeah! That’s how we do it,” he exclaimed to his engineer Peter Bonnington.“Another small step,” the Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, told Antonelli over the radio after the victory. “Another small step.”Quick GuideHow the title races standShowDrivers' standings1Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes365pts2George Russell 🇬🇧Mercedes2423Lewis Hamilton 🇬🇧Ferrari2414Max Verstappen 🇳🇱Red Bull2365Charles Leclerc 🇲🇨Ferrari2336Lando Norris 🇬🇧McLaren2117Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren1448Isack Hadjar🇫🇷Red Bull1059Liam Lawson🇳🇿Racing Bulls7710Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine4211Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls3812Franco Colapinto🇦🇷Alpine2713Oliver Bearman 🇬🇧Haas2314Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi1315Gabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷Audi1016Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas717Fernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston Martin718Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams719Alexander Albon🇹🇭Williams520Yuki Tsunoda🇯🇵Racing Bulls1Yet to score:Lance Stroll🇨🇦Aston MartinValtteri Bottas🇫🇮CadillacSergio Pérez🇲🇽CadillacConstructors' standings1Mercedes🇩🇪 607pts2Ferrari🇮🇹 4743Red Bull🇦🇹 3554McLaren🇬🇧3555Racing Bulls🇮🇹 1026Alpine🇫🇷 697Haas🇺🇸 308Audi🇩🇪 239Williams🇬🇧1210Aston Martin🇬🇧711Cadillac🇺🇸 0Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.With Mercedes having worked hard to iron outissues with their recent upgradesto the car, the victory was important to the team, who pulled off a coup in opting for a one-stop strategy which paid off handsomely for their world champion-elect driver. Antonelli paid tribute to his team.“We’re very close [to the title], hopefully we can clinch it soon,” he said. “It was a result we needed, to be fair, the whole team deserved it all this time – working to bring this new package and finally seeing the result is very pleasant. It was a perfect execution of strategy to call the one stop. Today was a great team effort.”This view was echoed by the Mercedes deputy team principal, Bradley Lord. “It felt like everyone was getting a bit excited but all Kimi could do today is go out and win,” he said. “Amazing job by everyone on the pit wall and the strategists back at base. What a drive, what a win.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHowever Verstappen, whose Red Bull team opted for a two-stop strategy, was far from enamoured with his afternoon and a car that was suffering from problems. “Yeah, that was terrible,” he said. “The pace, the wrong tyre, shit pit stop, shit engine braking. Nothing worked.”Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Formula OneMotor sportKimi AntonelliMercedes GPnewsShareReuse this content

title: Joe Marchant recalled to England training squad for Nations Championship | England rugby union team | The Guardian
description: Joe Marchant has been recalled to England’s training squad for the Nations Championship next month as Steve Borthwick faces injury disruption to his midfield options
Author: Luke McLaughlin
Headline: Joe Marchant has been recalled to England’s training squad for the Nations Championship next month as Steve Borthwick faces injury disruption to his midfield options
Content: Joe Marchant returned to the Prem with Sale this season after two years with Stade Français.Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Sale SharksView image in fullscreenJoe Marchant returned to the Prem with Sale this season after two years with Stade Français.Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Sale SharksEngland rugby union teamJoe Marchant recalled to England training squad for Nations ChampionshipSale centre returns after ending his two-year spell in FranceGloucester’s Will Joseph also in Steve Borthwick’s 36-man squadLuke McLaughlinSun 25 Oct 2026 13.57 EDTLast modified on Sun 25 Oct 2026 18.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSale’s Joe Marchant and Gloucester’s Will Joseph are two notable inclusions among Steve Borthwick’s 36-man England squad, announced on Sunday, for the conclusion of theNations Championshipin November, with both boosting the head coach’s midfield options.The 30-year-old centre Marchant last appeared for England at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, and spent two seasons at Stade Français in the Top 14, before returning to the Prem with Sale Sharks for this season.Will Joseph, the 24-year-old younger brother of the former England player Jonathan Joseph, has illuminated the table-topping Gloucester’s strong start to the domestic season. He was called up by Eddie Jones for the tour to Australia in 2022, making one brief appearance off the bench in a second-Test win against the Wallabies in Brisbane.Henry Slade, Max Ojomoh and Fraser Dingwall are Borthwick’s other centre options, with Benhard Janse van Rensburg of Bristol sidelined by a concussion sustained against Northampton this month. The Gloucester centre Charlie Atkinson is among three players called up to continue their injury rehabilitation, along with Manny Feyi-Waboso of Exeter and Bath’s Guy Pepper.The scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet, who helped Leicester to defeat their local rivals Northampton at Welford Road on Saturday, is included along with the Saints pair of Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland.Quick GuideEngland training squadShowForwards: F Baxter (Harlequins), O Chessum (Leicester Tigers), A Clark (Gloucester), A Coles (Northampton), L Cowan-Dickie (Sale), B Curry (Sale), T Curry (Sale), B Earl (Saracens), G Fisilau (Exeter Chiefs), J George (Saracens), E Genge (Bristol), J Heyes (Leicester), M Itoje (Saracens), E Iyogun (Northampton), G Martin (Saracens), A Opoku-Fordjour (Sale Sharks), T Pearson (Northampton), H Pollock (Northampton), W Stuart (Bath), K Tuipulotu (Bath).Backs: N Caluori (Saracens), F Dingwall (Northampton), G Ford (Sale), T Freeman (Northampton), G Furbank (Harlequins), W Joseph (Gloucester), J Marchant (Sale), A McParland (Northampton), A Mitchell (Northampton), C Murley (Harlequins), M Ojomoh (Bath), H Slade (Exeter), F Smith (Northampton), M Smith (Harlequins), F Steward (Leicester), J van Poortvliet (Leicester), Rehabilitation: S Atkinson (Gloucester), I Feyi-Waboso (Exeter), G Pepper (Bath).Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.The 21-year old McParland is uncapped, while there is no place in the squad for Ben Spencer of Bath. Kepu Tuipulotu, the Bath hooker, is another uncapped 21-year-old called up by Borthwick.Fin Smith, Marcus Smith and George Ford are the specialist fly‑halves – while in the forwards the captain, Maro Itoje, having been rested in the summer, will return to the international stage. Alex Coles, Ollie Chessum, George Martin and Arthur Clark, another player flourishing at Gloucester, will be candidates to start with Itoje at lock. But there is no place for the 37-year-old lock Courtney Lawes, who like Marchant returned from a spell in France to sign for Sale.Tom Pearson (Northampton) and Ben Curry (Sale) return to a squad packed with back-row talent, and will compete for starting spots with Tom Curry, Ben Earl, Henry Pollock and Greg Fisilau.The prop Fin Baxter, who impressed for Harlequins in their victory against Saracens on Sunday, is back after almost a year sidelined with a foot injury. His clubmate Marcus Smith made a strong case to start in November by dismantling Saracens in Quins’ 33-15 win.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBorthwick’s squad assembled on Sunday at Pennyhill Park for a three‑day training camp, with the players due to return to their clubs for the Prem’s fifth round next weekend.England begin their November programme against Australia at Twickenham on Sunday 8 November, before facing Japan on Saturday 14 November. A high-stakes encounter against the All Blacks follows on Saturday 21 November, with fixtures for the concluding Nations Championship weekend, on 27/28/29 November, to be confirmed.Explore more on these topicsEngland rugby union teamSteve BorthwickNations ChampionshipRugby unionnewsShareReuse this content
